# Introduction

When a Kona Low storm hits Hawaiʻi, heavy rain washes fertilizer, cesspool nutrients, and volcanic soil off the land and into the ocean. Does that change coastal water quality in a meaningful way — and if so, where, how much, and can we predict it from a map?

This report uses 694 water samples collected across four islands immediately after the March 2026 Kona Low to answer those questions. Interpolated maps show where nutrient concentrations were highest. A grouping analysis (PAM clustering) sorts sites into four distinct water types — from clean open-ocean water to freshwater plumes at stream mouths — and measures how different their chemistry is. A random forest model then asks whether those water types could have been predicted from landscape features alone: how close is a site to a stream mouth? To a cesspool? How much of the surrounding land is paved or farmed? How much water actually flowed through the nearest stream gauge in March? The model correctly classifies 67% of sites (vs 36% for a random guess), with stream mouth proximity, cesspool distance, and actual March discharge as the three strongest predictors.

# Data overview

```{r}
#| label: load-data
chem <- read_csv("data/clean_chemdata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  # Normalise apostrophe variants (ʻokina U+02BB, smart quotes U+2018/9) to
  # plain ASCII apostrophe so island-name joins are consistent throughout
  mutate(island = stringr::str_replace_all(island, "[\u02BB\u02BC\u2018\u2019]", "'")) |>
  # Ahupuaʻa assignment (spatial join pre-computed in 01_load_clean_data.R)
  left_join(
    read_csv("data/ahupuaa_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  # Distance to nearest cesspool per sample
  left_join(
    read_csv("data/sample_cesspool_distances.csv", show_col_types = FALSE),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) |>
  # Cesspool density per ahupuaʻa (join on ahupuaa + moku to avoid duplicate
  # ahupuaʻa names appearing in multiple moku / islands)
  left_join(
    read_csv("data/cesspool_by_ahupuaa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      select(ahupuaa, moku, cesspool_density_per_km2, n_cesspools),
    by = c("ahupuaa", "moku")
  )
```

`r nrow(chem)` samples collected across `r n_distinct(chem$island)` islands between `r format(min(chem$collected_hst, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %d, %Y")` and `r format(max(chem$collected_hst, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %d, %Y")`. Cesspool density is unavailable for Lānaʻi (no public data) and `r chem |> filter(island != "L\u0101na'i", is.na(cesspool_density_per_km2)) |> nrow()` samples on other islands where the ahupuaʻa is not in the cesspool dataset.

# Nutrient hotspot maps

Each map shows a kriged surface of NO₃+NO₂ (µmol/L) interpolated from coastal water samples collected after the storm. White circles mark sample collection points. The fill scale is logarithmic (log₁p) to show the full range of values without the highest concentrations washing out the spatial pattern. Land is masked in gray.

```{r}
#| label: helpers

normalize_name <- function(x) {
  x |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[\u02BB\u2018\u2019']", "") |>  # strip okina/smart quotes
    stringr::str_replace_all("\u0101", "a") |>                 # ā → a
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_trim()
}

# Shared island colour palette — ASCII apostrophes throughout for consistent matching
island_pal <- c(
  "O'ahu"    = "#1565C0",
  "Maui"     = "#2E7D32",
  "Moloka'i" = "#E65100",
  "Lāna'i"   = "#6A1B9A"
)

# Canonical recode: plain cache names → display names (matching island_pal keys).
# Use as: mutate(island = recode_island[island])
recode_island <- c(
  "Oahu"    = "O'ahu",
  "Maui"    = "Maui",
  "Molokai" = "Moloka'i",
  "Lanai"   = "L\u0101na'i"
)

# Scale metadata for each plottable variable. Add entries here to support new variables.
# `trans` drives both the internal kriging transform and the ggplot scale transform.
# `oob_label` is the label used for the top break (values squished above the limit).
var_meta <- list(
  NO3NO2 = list(
    label     = "NO\u2083+NO\u2082\n(\u03bcmol/L)",
   # limits    = c(0, 20),
  #  breaks    = c(0.5, 1, 3, 10, 20),
   # labels    = c("0.5", "1", "3", "10", "\u226520"),
     limits    = c(0, 10),
    breaks    = c(0.5, 1, 3, 5, 10),
    labels    = c("0.5", "1", "3", "5", "\u226510"),
     trans     = "log1p",
    direction = 1
  ),
  PO4 = list(
    label     = "PO\u2084\n(\u03bcmol/L)",
    limits    = c(0, 1),
    breaks    = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1),
    labels    = c("0.05", "0.1", "0.3", "0.5", "\u22651"),
    trans     = "log1p",
    direction = 1
  ),
  SiO2 = list(
    label     = "SiO\u2082\n(\u03bcmol/L)",
   # limits    = c(0, 100),
  #  breaks    = c(1, 5, 20, 50, 100),
  #  labels    = c("1", "5", "20", "50", "\u2265100"),
     limits    = c(0, 50),
    breaks    = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 50),
    labels    = c("1", "5", "10", "20", "\u226550"),
    trans     = "log1p",
    direction = 1
  ),
  NH3 = list(
    label     = "NH\u2083\n(\u03bcmol/L)",
    limits    = c(0, 3),
    breaks    = c(0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    labels    = c("0.1", "0.5", "1", "2", "\u22653"),
    trans     = "log1p",
    direction = 1
  ),
  Salinity = list(
    label     = "Salinity\n(PSU)",
    limits    = c(28, 36),
    breaks    = c(28, 30, 32, 34, 36),
    labels    = c("\u226428", "30", "32", "34", "36"),
    trans     = "identity",
    direction = -1
  )
)

krige_island_map <- function(data, island_name, ahupuaa_sf,
                              var = "NO3NO2",
                              res_m = 250, band_km = 3, tile_zoom = 11) {
  
  meta    <- var_meta[[var]]
  use_log <- !is.null(meta) && meta$trans == "log1p"
  if (is.null(meta)) meta <- list(
    label = var, limits = NULL, breaks = waiver(), labels = waiver(), trans = "identity"
  )
  
  island_data <- data |>
    filter(island == island_name, !is.na(.data[[var]]), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))
  
  # Dissolve ahupuaʻa polygons; drop parts < 1 km² to remove errant geometry
  match_idx <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_sf$mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)
  land_union <- ahupuaa_sf[match_idx, ] |>
    st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |> st_union()
  land_parts <- st_cast(land_union, "POLYGON")
  land_union  <- land_parts[as.numeric(st_area(land_parts)) > 1e6] |> st_union()
  land_sf_map <- st_as_sf(st_sf(geometry = land_union))
  
  coast_outer <- st_buffer(land_union, dist = band_km * 1000)
  coast_band  <- st_difference(coast_outer, land_union)
  coast_bbox  <- st_bbox(coast_outer)
  
  # Deduplicate sample locations — duplicate coordinates cause a singular
  # kriging covariance matrix and NA predictions across the whole island
  pts_proj <- island_data |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604) |>
    mutate(raw_val = .data[[var]],
           log_val = if (use_log) log1p(raw_val) else raw_val,
           X = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1],
           Y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
    group_by(X, Y) |>
    summarise(log_val = mean(log_val, na.rm = TRUE),
              raw_val = mean(raw_val, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("X", "Y"), crs = 32604)
  
  # Display points clipped to coast_bbox; carries variable values for shared color scale
  pts_proj_all <- island_data |>
    filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604) |>
    mutate(val = .data[[var]],
           X   = st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
           Y   = st_coordinates(geometry)[,2]) |>
    filter(X >= coast_bbox["xmin"], X <= coast_bbox["xmax"],
           Y >= coast_bbox["ymin"], Y <= coast_bbox["ymax"])
  
  # Variogram with enforced minimum range of island_diag / 5
  v_emp       <- variogram(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj)
  init_psill  <- var(pts_proj$log_val, na.rm = TRUE)
  island_diag <- sqrt(diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")])^2 +
                      diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")])^2)
  v_auto <- tryCatch(
    fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(psill = init_psill * 0.8, model = "Sph",
                             range = island_diag / 5, nugget = init_psill * 0.2)),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  min_range <- island_diag / 5
  v_fit <- if (!is.null(v_auto) && v_auto$range[2] >= min_range) v_auto else {
    psill  <- if (!is.null(v_auto)) v_auto$psill[2] else init_psill * 0.8
    nugget <- if (!is.null(v_auto)) v_auto$psill[1] else init_psill * 0.2
    vgm(psill = psill, model = "Sph", range = min_range, nugget = nugget)
  }
  
  # Prediction grid: coastal band intersected with a buffer around sample points.
  # Grid cells farther than min_range from any sample are excluded — no data
  # nearby means no interpolation shown (prevents extrapolation into unsurveyed coast).
  sample_coverage <- st_buffer(st_union(pts_proj), dist = min_range)
  grid_pts <- st_make_grid(coast_band, cellsize = res_m, what = "centers") |>
    st_as_sf() |>
    st_filter(coast_band) |>
    st_filter(sample_coverage)
  
  k_out <- suppressWarnings(
    krige(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj, grid_pts, model = v_fit, nmax = 40)
  )
  pred_df <- st_coordinates(k_out) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(pred = if (use_log) expm1(k_out$var1.pred) else k_out$var1.pred)
  
  krige_label <- if (use_log) paste0("log1p(", var, ")") else var
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster_rgb(data = get_tiles(st_transform(coast_outer, 4326),
                                         provider = "Esri.WorldImagery", zoom = tile_zoom)) +
    geom_raster(data = pred_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = pred), alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_sf(data = land_sf_map, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_sf(data = pts_proj_all, aes(fill = val), size = 1.0, shape = 21,
            color = "white", stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      name      = meta$label,
      option    = "plasma",
      direction = meta$direction,
      trans     = meta$trans,
      limits    = meta$limits,
      breaks    = meta$breaks,
      labels    = meta$labels,
      oob       = scales::squish,
      na.value  = "transparent",
      guide     = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(10, "lines"),
                                 barwidth  = unit(0.6, "lines"),
                                 ticks.linewidth = 0.5)
    ) +
    coord_sf(crs = 32604,
             xlim = c(coast_bbox["xmin"], coast_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(coast_bbox["ymin"], coast_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = island_name,
         subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(pts_proj),
                           " unique locations | ordinary kriging on ", krige_label)) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))
}

raw_points_map <- function(data, island_name, ahupuaa_sf,
                            var = "NO3NO2", tile_zoom = 12) {
  
  meta <- var_meta[[var]]
  if (is.null(meta)) meta <- list(
    label = var, limits = NULL, breaks = waiver(), labels = waiver(), trans = "identity"
  )
  
  island_data <- data |>
    filter(island == island_name, !is.na(.data[[var]]), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
    mutate(val = .data[[var]]) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604)
  
  # Same land polygon logic as krige_island_map
  match_idx <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_sf$mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)
  land_union <- ahupuaa_sf[match_idx, ] |>
    st_transform(32604) |>
    st_make_valid() |>
    st_union()
  land_parts <- st_cast(land_union, "POLYGON")
  land_union  <- land_parts[as.numeric(st_area(land_parts)) > 1e6] |> st_union()
  land_sf_map <- st_as_sf(st_sf(geometry = land_union))
  
  coast_outer <- st_buffer(land_union, dist = 5000)
  coast_bbox  <- st_bbox(coast_outer)
  
  sat_tiles <- get_tiles(st_transform(coast_outer, 4326),
                         provider = "Esri.WorldImagery", zoom = tile_zoom)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster_rgb(data = sat_tiles) +
    geom_sf(data = land_sf_map, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_sf(data = island_data, aes(fill = val), size = 3.5, shape = 21,
            color = "white", stroke = 0.5, alpha = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      name      = meta$label,
      option    = "plasma",
      direction = meta$direction,
      trans     = meta$trans,
      limits    = meta$limits,
      breaks    = meta$breaks,
      labels    = meta$labels,
      oob       = scales::squish,
      guide     = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(8, "lines"),
                                 barwidth  = unit(0.6, "lines"),
                                 ticks.linewidth = 0.5)
    ) +
    coord_sf(crs = 32604,
             xlim = c(coast_bbox["xmin"], coast_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(coast_bbox["ymin"], coast_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = island_name,
         subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(island_data),
                           " samples | raw observations (insufficient coverage for kriging)")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))
}

# ── krige_surface_data: returns pred_df + land polygon + coast_bbox ───────────
krige_surface_data <- function(data, island_name, ahupuaa_sf,
                               var = "NO3NO2", res_m = 300, band_km = 3) {
  meta    <- var_meta[[var]]
  use_log <- !is.null(meta) && meta$trans == "log1p"
  island_data <- data |>
    filter(island == island_name, !is.na(.data[[var]]),
           !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))
  match_idx  <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_sf$mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)
  land_union <- ahupuaa_sf[match_idx, ] |>
    st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |> st_union()
  land_parts <- st_cast(land_union, "POLYGON")
  land_union <- land_parts[as.numeric(st_area(land_parts)) > 1e6] |> st_union()
  coast_outer <- st_buffer(land_union, dist = band_km * 1000)
  coast_band  <- st_difference(coast_outer, land_union)
  coast_bbox  <- st_bbox(coast_outer)
  pts_proj <- island_data |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604) |>
    mutate(raw_val = .data[[var]],
           log_val = if (use_log) log1p(raw_val) else raw_val,
           X = st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
           Y = st_coordinates(geometry)[,2]) |>
    group_by(X, Y) |>
    summarise(log_val = mean(log_val, na.rm = TRUE),
              raw_val = mean(raw_val, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("X","Y"), crs = 32604)
  island_diag <- sqrt(diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")])^2 +
                      diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")])^2)
  min_range <- island_diag / 5
  v_emp  <- variogram(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj)
  v_auto <- tryCatch(
    fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.8, "Sph",
                              min_range, var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.2)),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  v_fit <- if (!is.null(v_auto) && v_auto$range[2] >= min_range) v_auto else
    vgm(var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.8, "Sph", min_range, var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.2)
  sample_cov <- st_buffer(st_union(pts_proj), dist = min_range)
  grid_pts <- st_make_grid(coast_band, cellsize = res_m, what = "centers") |>
    st_as_sf() |> st_filter(coast_band) |> st_filter(sample_cov)
  k_out <- suppressWarnings(krige(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj, grid_pts, model = v_fit, nmax = 40))
  pred_df <- st_coordinates(k_out) |> as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(pred = if (use_log) expm1(k_out$var1.pred) else k_out$var1.pred)
  list(pred_df    = pred_df,
       land_sf    = st_as_sf(st_sf(geometry = land_union)),
       coast_bbox = coast_bbox)
}

# ── maui_validation_map: kriging surface + optional Hui station overlay ───────
# Pass bg_hui_loc to show Hui triangles (only meaningful for var = "NO3NO2").
maui_validation_map <- function(data, ahupuaa_sf, var = "NO3NO2",
                                 bg_hui_loc = NULL, tile_zoom = 11) {
  meta <- var_meta[[var]]
  if (is.null(meta)) meta <- list(
    label = var, limits = NULL, breaks = waiver(), labels = waiver(),
    trans = "identity", direction = 1
  )

  kd     <- krige_surface_data(data, "Maui", ahupuaa_sf, var = var)
  cs_pts <- data |>
    filter(island == "Maui", !is.na(.data[[var]]), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
    mutate(val = .data[[var]]) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604)
  sat <- get_tiles(
    st_as_sfc(kd$coast_bbox) |> st_set_crs(32604) |> st_transform(4326),
    provider = "Esri.WorldImagery", zoom = tile_zoom
  )

  # Build Hui station sf internally when bg_hui_loc is supplied
  # Map chem var names to the corresponding Hui column (all in µmol/L)
  hui_col_map <- c(NO3NO2 = "NNN_umol", PO4 = "Phosphate_umol",
                   SiO2   = "Silicate_umol", NH3 = "NH4_umol")
  hui_col  <- hui_col_map[var]
  show_hui <- !is.null(bg_hui_loc) && !is.na(hui_col) && hui_col %in% names(bg_hui_loc)

  if (show_hui) {
    hui_post <- bg_hui_loc |>
      filter(year(Date) == 2026, month(Date) == 3,
             Date >= as.Date("2026-03-14"), !is.na(.data[[hui_col]])) |>
      group_by(Station, SiteName, region, Lat, Long) |>
      summarise(val_umol = mean(.data[[hui_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    hui_hist_med <- bg_hui_loc |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[hui_col]])) |>
      group_by(Station) |>
      summarise(med_hist = median(.data[[hui_col]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    log_lo   <- log1p(1); log_hi <- log1p(20)
    grey_pal <- colorRampPalette(c("gray20", "white"))(1000)
    hui_sf <- bg_hui_loc |>
      distinct(Station, SiteName, region, Lat, Long) |>
      filter(!is.na(Lat), !is.na(Long)) |>
      left_join(hui_post |> select(Station, val_umol), by = "Station") |>
      left_join(hui_hist_med, by = "Station") |>
      mutate(
        fold_change = val_umol / med_hist,
        fc_safe     = pmin(pmax(replace_na(fold_change, 1), 1), 20),
        tri_fill    = grey_pal[round((log1p(fc_safe) - log_lo) /
                                       (log_hi - log_lo) * 999) + 1],
        tri_fill    = case_when(
          is.na(fold_change) & !is.na(med_hist) ~ "gray50",
          is.na(med_hist)                        ~ "gray70",
          TRUE                                   ~ tri_fill
        ),
        fold_change = replace_na(fold_change, 1)
      ) |>
      st_as_sf(coords = c("Long","Lat"), crs = 4326) |>
      st_transform(32604)
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatraster_rgb(data = sat) +
    geom_raster(data = kd$pred_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = pred), alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_sf(data = kd$land_sf, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_sf(data = cs_pts, aes(fill = val),
            shape = 21, size = 1.0, color = "white", stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.5)

  # fill scale used only for kriging raster + CS circles (plasma)
  p <- p +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      name      = meta$label,
      option    = "plasma",
      direction = meta$direction,
      trans     = meta$trans,
      limits    = meta$limits,
      breaks    = meta$breaks,
      labels    = meta$labels,
      oob       = scales::squish,
      na.value  = "transparent",
      guide     = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(10, "lines"),
                                 barwidth  = unit(0.6, "lines"),
                                 ticks.linewidth = 0.5)
    )

  if (show_hui) {
    hui_breaks <- c(1, 3, 5, 10, 20)
    hui_labels <- c("1", "3", "5", "10", "\u226520")
    hui_name   <- "Fold-change\n(Mar 2026 /\nall-time median)"
    p <- p +
      # Shape 24 (fill + white outline); I() bypasses the plasma fill scale
      geom_sf(data = hui_sf,
              aes(size = fold_change, fill = I(tri_fill)),
              color = "white", shape = 24, stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.85) +
      ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
        data = hui_sf |> filter(fold_change > 15),
        aes(label    = paste0(SiteName, "\n", round(fold_change, 0), "\u00d7"),
            geometry = geometry),
        stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#B71C1C",
        fill = alpha("white", 0.85), label.size = 0.2,
        nudge_y = 4500, min.segment.length = 0
      ) +
      scale_size_continuous(
        name = hui_name, range = c(1.0, 8), limits = c(1, 20),
        breaks = hui_breaks, labels = hui_labels,
        guide = guide_legend(
          theme = theme(legend.key = element_rect(fill = "gray30", color = NA)),
          override.aes = list(shape = 24, color = "white", stroke = 0.8, alpha = 0.85,
                              fill = c("#333333", "#6F6F6F", "#929292", "#C6C6C6", "#FFFFFF"))
        )
      )
  }

  hui_note <- if (show_hui) {
    paste0("    \u25b3 Hui o Ka Wai Ola stations (size = Mar 2026 fold-change above all-time median)\n",
           "\u25b3 small = no March 2026 sample    \u25b3 gray = insufficient data    ",
           "Labels: stations with fold-change > 15\u00d7")
  } else ""

  p +
    coord_sf(crs = 32604,
             xlim = c(kd$coast_bbox["xmin"], kd$coast_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(kd$coast_bbox["ymin"], kd$coast_bbox["ymax"]),
             expand = FALSE) +
    labs(
  #    subtitle = paste0("\u25cf community science samples (this study)", hui_note),
      caption  = if (show_hui) "Hui data: Falinski et al. / Hui o Ka Wai Ola." else NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.title    = element_blank(),
      axis.text     = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "gray40"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}
```

## O'ahu

Oʻahu's highest nutrient concentrations cluster along the northwestern (Waiʻanae) coast and around Pearl Harbor, consistent with those areas having both dense cesspool infrastructure and streams that drain heavily developed land. The salinity map shows freshwater dilution in the same locations, confirming this is land-sourced water, not re-suspended sediment.

```{r}
#| label: map-oahu
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Spatially interpolated nutrient and salinity maps for Oʻahu, March 2026. Color shows concentration — yellow-green = highest, dark purple = lowest (all log scale). Circles are individual sample points colored on the same scale. Low-salinity (freshwater-diluted) hotspots on the northwest coast line up with the highest nitrogen and silica readings."
oahuNN<-krige_island_map(chem, "O'ahu", ahupuaa_raw,var = "NO3NO2" )

oahuPO<-krige_island_map(chem, "O'ahu", ahupuaa_raw,var ="PO4" )

oahuNH3<-krige_island_map(chem, "O'ahu", ahupuaa_raw,var ="NH3" )

oahuSal<-krige_island_map(chem, "O'ahu", ahupuaa_raw,var ="Salinity" )

(oahuNN|oahuPO|oahuNH3)/(oahuSi|oahuSal|plot_spacer())
ggsave(here("output","Oahu_spatial.png"), height = 12, width = 18)

```

## Maui

Maui shows the most dramatic hotspot signal of any island, concentrated on the north and west coasts. The Mālā Ramp area and Honoköwai in West Maui stand out clearly — these sites also showed the largest departures from their long-term monitoring baselines (see Hui comparison below). North Maui's windward streams drain some of the island's most intensively farmed land, explaining the particularly high silica (SiO₂) signature there.

The match between low-salinity patches and high-nutrient zones confirms that dilution with freshwater runoff is driving the signal, not local biological processes."

# Independent validation: Hui o Ka Wai Ola stations on the Maui kriging surface

The kriging surface is derived entirely from community science samples. The Hui o Ka Wai Ola programme provides an independent check: do the long-term fixed stations — sampled with laboratory-grade methods over a decade — agree with where the community science kriging shows hotspots? Triangles show Hui station post-storm NO₃+NO₂ on the same color scale as the kriging surface; their colors should match the surface underneath them if the two datasets are consistent.

```{r}
#| label: maui-validation-map
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Two independent datasets, one picture. Background: the interpolated nitrogen (NO₃+NO₂) map built from community science samples. Triangles: Hui o Ka Wai Ola professional monitoring stations, colored by their own post-storm measurements (same color scale). Gray-outlined triangles had no March 2026 sample. The Hui stations with the most extreme readings — Mālā Ramp (43×), Camp Olowalu (32×), and others on West Maui — sit precisely where the community science map shows the darkest hotspot colors. The agreement between two completely independent datasets confirms the hotspot pattern is real."


bg_hui_loc <- bind_rows(
  readxl::read_excel(
    "data/background_nutrients/hui-south-maui-thru-2026-1st-quarter.0.xlsx",
    sheet = "data") |>
    mutate(Turbidity = as.numeric(Turbidity), region = "South Maui"),
  readxl::read_excel(
    "data/background_nutrients/hui-west-maui-thru-2026-1st-quarter.0.xlsx",
    sheet = "data") |>
    mutate(Turbidity = as.numeric(Turbidity), region = "West Maui")
) |>
  mutate(Date           = as.Date(Date),
         NNN_umol       = as.numeric(NNN)       / 14.007,   # µg/L N  → µmol/L
         Phosphate_umol = as.numeric(Phosphate) / 30.974,   # µg/L P  → µmol/L
         Silicate_umol  = as.numeric(Silicate)  / 28.086,   # µg/L Si → µmol/L
         NH4_umol       = as.numeric(NH4)        / 14.007)  # µg/L N  → µmol/L

HuiNN<-maui_validation_map(chem, ahupuaa_raw, var = "NO3NO2", bg_hui_loc = bg_hui_loc)

HuiSi<-maui_validation_map(chem, ahupuaa_raw, var = "SiO2", bg_hui_loc = bg_hui_loc)

HuiNH3<-maui_validation_map(chem, ahupuaa_raw, var = "NH3", bg_hui_loc = bg_hui_loc)

HuiPO<-maui_validation_map(chem, ahupuaa_raw, var = "PO4", bg_hui_loc = bg_hui_loc)

no_sub  <- theme(plot.subtitle = element_blank(), plot.caption = element_blank())
no_size <- guides(size = "none")

size_legend <- get_legend(
  HuiNN + guides(fill = "none") + theme(legend.position = "right")
)

plot_grid(
  plot_grid(
    HuiNN  + no_size + no_sub,
    HuiPO  + no_size + no_sub,
    HuiNH3 + no_size + no_sub,
    HuiSi  + no_size + no_sub,
    ncol = 2
  ),
  size_legend,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1, 0.13)
) |>
  ggdraw() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

ggsave(here("output","hui_spatial.png"), height = 12, width = 12)
```

The Hui stations on West Maui's leeward coast show amber-to-orange colors, meaning their post-storm readings were 8–43× higher than their own ten-year averages. The calmer eastern coast shows lower readings in both datasets. The fact that community science volunteers and trained monitoring staff — sampling at different times with different equipment — independently found the same hotspot pattern in the same places gives us high confidence the signal is real, not a measurement artifact.

# Storm cascade: disruption of coastal biogeochemistry

The storm set off a four-step chain of events visible in satellite data, stream gauges, and water chemistry. Rain (panel A) filled streams (panel B), which flushed nutrients into the coast, triggering an algae bloom visible from space (panel C), and leaving elevated chemical concentrations still measurable when volunteers sampled two weeks later (panel D). Peak rainfall hit March 13–14, reaching 42–100 mm/day averaged across each island. Streams responded immediately, with peak flows of 231–1,040 cubic feet per second depending on watershed size. Coastal chlorophyll — a measure of algae growth — rose across all three islands within days and remained elevated for weeks. When community scientists sampled in late March and early April, nitrogen (NO₃+NO₂) and silica (SiO₂) were the most clearly elevated nutrients, consistent with runoff from volcanic soils.

```{r}
#| label: storm-cascade-figure
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "Rain → streams → algae → chemistry: the full storm cascade in four panels. (A) Average daily rainfall per island from atmospheric model data (NCEP). (B) Stream discharge at three USGS gauges — Makaha Stream (Oʻahu), Halawa Stream (Molokaʻi), Hanawi Stream (Maui) — on a log scale because flows span three orders of magnitude. (C) Mean coastal chlorophyll-a from satellite (VIIRS NOAA-20), with a smoothed trend line; individual daily averages shown as points (only days with ≥8 valid satellite pixels included). (D) Post-storm nutrient concentrations by island from community science sampling (Mar 28–Apr 8). Blue shading = the Kona Low storm window (Mar 10–25); green shading = sampling window."



# ── shared constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────
storm_xmin <- as.Date("2026-03-10"); storm_xmax <- as.Date("2026-03-25")
samp_xmin  <- as.Date("2026-03-28"); samp_xmax  <- as.Date("2026-04-08")
plot_xlim  <- as.Date(c("2026-01-15", "2026-06-05"))

windows <- list(
  annotate("rect", xmin = storm_xmin, xmax = storm_xmax,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#BBDEFB", alpha = 0.75),
  annotate("rect", xmin = samp_xmin,  xmax = samp_xmax,
           ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#C8E6C9", alpha = 0.75)
)

ts_base <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x       = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x       = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.margin        = margin(3, 6, 1, 6),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(size = 8.5)
  )

# Panel A: Rainfall
rain_df <- read_csv("hawaii_ncep_janjun_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(island %in% c("Oahu", "Maui", "Molokai"),
         date >= plot_xlim[1], date <= plot_xlim[2]) |>
  mutate(island = recode_island[island]) |>
  group_by(island, date) |>
  summarise(precip_mm = mean(precip_mmday, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

pA <- ggplot(rain_df, aes(x = date, y = precip_mm, fill = island, color = island)) +
  windows +
  geom_area(position = "identity", alpha = 0.30, linewidth = 0.35) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-02-17"), y = 172,
           label = "Feb event", size = 2.6, color = "gray35", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2026-03-17"), y = 108,
           label = "Kona Low", size = 2.6, color = "#1A237E", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = island_pal) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal) +
  scale_x_date(limits = plot_xlim, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(y = "Rainfall\n(mm/day)", tag = "A") +
  ts_base

# Panel B: Stream discharge (USGS NWIS — cached in data/usgs_discharge_cache.rds)
gauge_meta <- tibble(
  site_no = c("16211600", "16400000", "16508000"),
  island  = c("O'ahu",    "Moloka'i", "Maui")
)

dis_df <- read_csv("data/usgs_discharge_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types = cols(site_no = col_character())) |>
  dataRetrieval::renameNWISColumns() |>
  filter(site_no %in% gauge_meta$site_no,
         Date >= plot_xlim[1], Date <= plot_xlim[2], Flow > 0.5) |>
  left_join(gauge_meta, by = "site_no")

pB <- ggplot(dis_df, aes(x = Date, y = Flow, color = island, group = site_no)) +
  windows +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65, alpha = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal) +
  scale_x_date(limits = plot_xlim, date_labels = "%b %Y", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 10, 100, 1000),
                labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.8, 3000)) +
  labs(y = "Discharge\n(cfs, log)", tag = "B") +
  ts_base +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.3)
  )

# Panel C: Coastal chlorophyll (VIIRS NOAA-20 — cached in hawaii_chlorophyll_cache.rds)
chla_df <- readRDS("hawaii_chlorophyll_cache.rds") |>    # satellite array — kept as RDS
  filter(island %in% c("Oahu", "Maui", "Molokai"),
         date >= plot_xlim[1], date <= plot_xlim[2]) |>
  mutate(island = recode_island[island]) |>
  group_by(island, date) |>
  summarise(mean_chla = mean(chlor_a, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_valid   = sum(!is.na(chlor_a)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_valid >= 8, mean_chla > 0)

pC <- ggplot(chla_df, aes(x = date, y = mean_chla, color = island)) +
  windows +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.55, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", span = 0.2, se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(limits = plot_xlim, date_labels = "%b %Y", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10),
                labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(y = "Chlorophyll-a\n(mg/m\u00b3, log)", tag = "C") +
  ts_base +
  theme(
    axis.text.x      = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.ticks.x     = element_line(linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin      = margin(1, 6, 2, 6)
  )

# Panel D: Post-storm nutrient distributions
nut_long <- chem |>
  filter(island %in% c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i")) |>
  mutate(
    island = factor(island, levels = c("Maui", "Moloka'i", "O'ahu"))
  ) |>

pD <- ggplot(nut_long, aes(x = island, y = conc, fill = island, color = island)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.28, linewidth = 0.3, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.17, outliers = FALSE,
               fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = island_pal) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = label_parsed) +
  labs(tag = "D", y = expression(paste(mu, "mol L"^{-1})), x = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = rel(0.85)),
    strip.text         = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.margin        = margin(4, 8, 4, 2),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(size = 8.5)
  )

# Assemble
((pA / pB) | pD) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(3, 1.5)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = "Kona Low storm cascade: terrestrial runoff disrupts coastal biogeochemistry",
    caption = paste0(
      "Blue shading = Kona Low storm window (Mar 10\u201325).  ",
      "Green shading = community science sampling (Mar 28\u2013Apr 8).\n",
      "",
      "Stream gauges: Makaha Str (O\u02BBahu), Halawa Str (Moloka\u02BBi), Hanawi Str (Maui)."
    ),
    theme = theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "gray40",
                                  hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 6)),
      plot.margin  = margin(8, 8, 6, 8)
```

# Spatial structure of the biogeochemical signal

If the storm's chemical impact was driven by watershed runoff, then nearby coastal sites should have more similar nutrient levels than sites far apart — high readings near stream mouths, lower readings away from them. This would produce a non-random, geographically coherent pattern. We test this with Moran's I, a standard measure of spatial clustering where a positive, statistically significant value means nearby sites are more alike than you'd expect by chance. The test was run separately for each nutrient and island using the eight nearest sampling neighbours. Lāna'i had too few samples and is excluded.

```{r}
#| label: morans-i
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Do high-nutrient sites cluster together spatially? Moran's I measures this: values above zero (filled points, p < 0.05) mean nearby sites are more similar than random chance would produce; open circles are not statistically distinguishable from random. Error bars = ±1.96 standard errors. SiO₂ and NO₃+NO₂ show clear geographic clustering on both Maui and Molokaʻi — their hotspots follow the shape of watersheds and stream mouths. NH₃ shows no significant clustering, meaning it is scattered randomly across the coast rather than concentrated near any particular landscape feature."

nutrients  <- c("SiO2", "NO3NO2", "PO4", "NH3")
islands    <- c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i")

chem_sf_mi <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude), !is.na(island)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

moran_results <- purrr::map_dfr(islands, function(isl) {
  purrr::map_dfr(nutrients, function(nut) {
    pts <- chem_sf_mi |> filter(island == isl, !is.na(.data[[nut]]))
    if (nrow(pts) < 15) return(NULL)
    nb <- knn2nb(knearneigh(st_coordinates(pts), k = 8), sym = TRUE)
    lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
    mt <- moran.test(pts[[nut]], lw, zero.policy = TRUE, alternative = "greater")
    tibble(
      island   = isl,
      nutrient = nut,
      n        = nrow(pts),
      moran_I  = unname(mt$estimate["Moran I statistic"]),
      expected = unname(mt$estimate["Expectation"]),
      variance = unname(mt$estimate["Variance"]),
      p_value  = mt$p.value
    )
  })
})

# Plot
nutrient_labels_mi <- c(
  "SiO2"   = "SiO[2]",
  "NO3NO2" = "NO[3]+NO[2]",
  "PO4"    = "PO[4]",
  "NH3"    = "NH[3]"
)

moran_results |>
  mutate(
    island   = factor(island,   levels = c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i")),
    nutrient = factor(nutrient, levels = nutrients),
    sig_label = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "p < 0.001",
      p_value < 0.01  ~ "p < 0.01",
      p_value < 0.05  ~ "p < 0.05",
      TRUE            ~ "n.s."
    ),
    sig_label = factor(sig_label,
      levels = c("p < 0.001", "p < 0.01", "p < 0.05", "n.s."))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = moran_I, y = nutrient, color = island, shape = sig_label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = moran_I - 1.96 * sqrt(variance),
        xmax = moran_I + 1.96 * sqrt(variance)),
    width = 0, linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.35,
    orientation = "y",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("p < 0.001" = 16, "p < 0.01" = 17, "p < 0.05" = 15, "n.s." = 1),
    name   = "Significance"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.05, 0.5), breaks = seq(0, 0.5, 0.1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) parse(text = nutrient_labels_mi[x])) +
  labs(
    x        = "Moran's I  (k = 8 nearest neighbours)",
    y        = NULL,
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate spatial clustering; error bars = ±1.96 SE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray90"),
    legend.position    = "right",
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: morans-i-table
moran_results |>
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      p_value < 0.001 ~ "***", p_value < 0.01 ~ "**",
      p_value < 0.05 ~ "*",   TRUE ~ "n.s."
    )
  ) |>
  select(Island = island, Nutrient = nutrient, n,
         `Moran's I` = moran_I, `p-value` = p_value, ` ` = sig) |>
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Moran's I spatial autocorrelation statistics per island and nutrient. Spatial weights: k = 8 nearest neighbours (UTM zone 4N). One-sided test against the alternative of positive spatial autocorrelation.")
```

Silica (SiO₂) shows the tightest geographic clustering on Maui (Moran's I = 0.41) and Molokaʻi (I = 0.40). Silica is a reliable marker of volcanic rock weathering — it enters the ocean almost exclusively through stream runoff, so its spatial pattern closely traces where streams met the coast during the storm. Nitrogen (NO₃+NO₂) clusters almost as strongly. Ammonium (NH₃), by contrast, shows no significant spatial pattern on either island — it appears scattered randomly across the coast. This contrast is telling: the storm stamped a watershed-shaped footprint on nitrogen and silica, but NH₃ — which builds up through biological decomposition in sediments — was unaffected by the event.

# Storm context: rainfall return period

Was this storm unusual? This matters enormously for interpretation: if the March 2026 Kona Low was a once-in-a-generation event, the chemical impacts it caused might be rare too. If it was an ordinary storm, those same impacts are happening every year — they've just never been measured at this scale before.

```{r}
#| label: storm-return-period
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Was the March 2026 Kona Low unusual? No. Boxes show the range of March monthly rainfall across years (2013–2025) from satellite-based rainfall estimates (CHIRPS). Diamonds show March 2026 — estimated from atmospheric model data (NCEP) and scaled to match the CHIRPS units. On all three islands, 2026 fell close to or slightly above the historical median: about half of past March events were wetter. Individual years are shown as dots (filled = wetter than 2026, open = drier)."

# ── Historical March monthly totals from CHIRPS (2013–2025) ─────────────────
# Cache stores monthly totals as one value per island per month (labeled day 1).
march_hist <- read_csv("hawaii_rainfall_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(source == "CHIRPS",
         island %in% c("Oahu","Maui","Molokai"),
         lubridate::month(date) == 3,
         lubridate::year(date) <= 2025) |>
  mutate(precip = if_else(precip < 0, NA_real_, precip)) |>
  group_by(island, year = lubridate::year(date)) |>
  summarise(march_mm = mean(precip, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# ── March 2026 monthly total: NCEP bias-corrected to CHIRPS scale ────────────
ncep_daily_rp <- read_csv("hawaii_ncep_janjun_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(island %in% c("Oahu","Maui","Molokai")) |>
  group_by(island, date) |>
  summarise(precip_mm = mean(precip_mmday, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Bias factor: ratio of CHIRPS to NCEP over Jan–Feb overlap (same months in cache)
chirps_jf <- read_csv("hawaii_rainfall_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(source == "CHIRPS",
         island %in% c("Oahu","Maui","Molokai"),
         lubridate::month(date) %in% c(1, 2),
         lubridate::year(date) >= 2013) |>
  mutate(precip = if_else(precip < 0, NA_real_, precip)) |>
  group_by(island, year = lubridate::year(date),
           month = lubridate::month(date)) |>
  summarise(chirps_mm = mean(precip, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ncep_jf <- ncep_daily_rp |>
  filter(lubridate::month(date) %in% c(1, 2),
         lubridate::year(date) >= 2013,
         date <= as.Date("2026-02-28")) |>
  group_by(island, year = lubridate::year(date),
           month = lubridate::month(date)) |>
  summarise(ncep_mm = sum(precip_mm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

bias_rp <- inner_join(chirps_jf, ncep_jf, by = c("island","year","month")) |>
  group_by(island) |>
  summarise(factor = mean(chirps_mm, na.rm = TRUE) /
                     mean(ncep_mm,   na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

storm_rp <- ncep_daily_rp |>
  filter(lubridate::year(date) == 2026, lubridate::month(date) == 3) |>
  group_by(island) |>
  summarise(ncep_march_mm = sum(precip_mm, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(bias_rp, by = "island") |>
  mutate(storm_mm = ncep_march_mm * factor)

# ── Recode plain cache names → display names before plotting ─────────────────
march_hist  <- march_hist  |> mutate(island = recode_island[island])
storm_rp    <- storm_rp    |> mutate(island = recode_island[island])

march_hist_storm <- march_hist |>
  left_join(storm_rp |> select(island, storm_mm), by = "island") |>
  mutate(above = march_mm >= storm_mm)

# Panel A: year-by-year dots + boxplot summary
pA_rp <- ggplot(march_hist, aes(x = island, y = march_mm,
                                 fill = island, color = island)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.25, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(aes(shape = march_hist_storm$above), width = 0.08,
              size = 2.3, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = storm_rp,
             aes(x = island, y = storm_mm),
             color = "black", fill = "white",
             size = 4.5, shape = 23, stroke = 1.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 16),
                     labels = c("Below 2026", "Above 2026"),
                     name   = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "March rainfall total (mm)",
       subtitle = "CHIRPS island-mean March totals 2013\u20132025 \u00b7 Diamond = March 2026 (NCEP, bias-corrected)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position    = "bottom",
        plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "gray40"))

pA_rp
```

March 2026 was an average March — slightly above the historical median on all three islands (Maui: `r round(storm_rp$storm_mm[storm_rp$island=="Maui"])` mm vs. the typical `r round(median(march_hist$march_mm[march_hist$island=="Maui"], na.rm=TRUE))` mm; Molokaʻi: `r round(storm_rp$storm_mm[storm_rp$island=="Moloka'i"])` vs. `r round(median(march_hist$march_mm[march_hist$island=="Moloka'i"], na.rm=TRUE))` mm; Oʻahu: `r round(storm_rp$storm_mm[storm_rp$island=="O'ahu"])` vs. `r round(median(march_hist$march_mm[march_hist$island=="O'ahu"], na.rm=TRUE))` mm), with stream gauge records confirming moderate, not record, flows. About half of past March events were wetter. **This is the most important finding in the report: the dramatic water-quality changes documented here — nutrients 3–6× above background, spatial hotspots at stream mouths, a measurable algae bloom — were caused by a perfectly ordinary Kona Low.** If an average storm does this, the same thing happens every year. These impacts are not rare — they have just never been measured at this spatial scale before.

---

# Land–sea connectivity: salinity–nutrient mixing

Salinity is a natural tracer of freshwater: the lower it is, the more land-sourced water is mixed in. If runoff from the storm is carrying the nutrients, we'd expect to see a clear pattern — the more freshwater at a site (lower salinity), the more nutrients. The plots below test this for all four measured nutrients. Sites with Sal ≤ 34 PSU are coloured orange (storm-influenced), while marine-background sites (Sal > 34 PSU) are blue. Zeros are excluded as below-detection readings.

```{r}
#| label: salinity-nutrient-mixing
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "As salinity drops (more freshwater mixing in), nutrients rise — but only for the nutrients carried by runoff. Orange points and trend line: storm-influenced sites (Sal ≤ 34 PSU). Blue points and horizontal line: marine-background sites (Sal > 34 PSU) shown at their median concentration. NO₃+NO₂ and SiO₂ show steep, consistent increases as sites become more freshwater-influenced — confirming that land-sourced water is delivering these nutrients. PO₄ shows a weaker version of the same pattern. NH₃ has a flat, scattered relationship, meaning it is not being delivered by runoff in the same way — it comes from other sources (biological breakdown in sediments) that are unrelated to how much freshwater is present."

sal_zone_pal <- c("Storm-influenced\n(\u2264 34 PSU)" = "#E65100",
                  "Marine background\n(> 34 PSU)"   = "#1565C0")

mixing_long <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(Salinity)) |>
  select(island, Salinity, NO3NO2, PO4, SiO2, NH3) |>
  pivot_longer(c(NO3NO2, PO4, SiO2, NH3),
               names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc), conc > 0) |>               # drop zeros (below detection)
  mutate(
    nutrient = factor(nutrient,
      levels = c("NO3NO2", "PO4", "SiO2", "NH3"),
      labels = c("NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (\u03bcmol/L)",
                 "PO\u2084 (\u03bcmol/L)",
                 "SiO\u2082 (\u03bcmol/L)",
                 "NH\u2083 (\u03bcmol/L)")),
    sal_zone = factor(
      if_else(Salinity > 34,
              "Marine background\n(> 34 PSU)",
              "Storm-influenced\n(\u2264 34 PSU)"),
      levels = c("Storm-influenced\n(\u2264 34 PSU)",
                 "Marine background\n(> 34 PSU)"))
  )

# Median nutrient concentration for marine background sites (horizontal reference)
marine_medians <- mixing_long |>
  filter(sal_zone == "Marine background\n(> 34 PSU)") |>
  group_by(nutrient) |>
  summarise(med = median(conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(mixing_long, aes(x = Salinity, y = conc, color = sal_zone)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 34, linetype = "dotted",
             color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_smooth(data = \(d) filter(d, sal_zone == "Storm-influenced\n(\u2264 34 PSU)"),
              method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.15,
              color = "#E65100") +
  geom_hline(data = marine_medians, aes(yintercept = med),
             color = "#1565C0", linetype = "solid", linewidth = 0.8,
             inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = sal_zone_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(NA, 36.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(x = "Salinity (PSU)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

**NO₃+NO₂ and SiO₂** behave as expected if they are coming from land runoff: concentrations fall steeply as salinity rises, and level off once water becomes fully marine. This is the textbook pattern for a land-sourced contaminant diluting into the ocean. **PO₄** follows the same pattern but also remains elevated in fully marine water — suggesting a chronic background phosphorus source (likely cesspools leaching through groundwater) beyond the storm signal alone. **NH₃** shows little relationship with salinity in either zone, confirming it is not being delivered by runoff and instead accumulates through biological processes in seafloor sediments.

# Methods

## Sampling

Water samples were collected by community volunteers and scientists across O'ahu, Maui, Moloka'i, and Lāna'i between `r format(min(chem$collected_hst, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %d")` and `r format(max(chem$collected_hst, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %d, %Y")`, following the March 2026 Kona Low storm. NO₃+NO₂ was analyzed colorimetrically.

## Spatial interpolation

Ordinary kriging was used to interpolate NO₃+NO₂ concentrations between sample locations for islands with sufficient coverage (O'ahu, Maui, Moloka'i). Kriging was performed in R using the `gstat` package. Prior to kriging, concentrations were log₁p-transformed (log(x + 1)) to stabilize variance and approximate normality — a standard approach for right-skewed geochemical data.

Where multiple samples were collected at the same GPS location, values were averaged prior to kriging — duplicate coordinates produce a singular covariance matrix that causes predictions to fail. An empirical variogram was computed for each island and fit with a spherical model. Because the auto-fit variogram range (~5–6 km) is driven by local sample clustering and leaves sections of the coastline with no near-neighbor data, a minimum range of 1/5 of the island's spatial diagonal is enforced to ensure gap-free predictions across the full coast. The prediction grid was constructed as a 3 km coastal band derived by buffering the island polygon outward and subtracting the land area, then further clipped to the union of sample-point buffers (radius = variogram range). This prevents kriging from extrapolating into unsurveyed coastal stretches. The 40 nearest neighbors were used for each prediction. Back-transformed predictions (expm1) are displayed on a log₁p color scale. Sample points are colored on the same scale as the kriging surface, so extreme observed values (e.g. 265 µmol/L on O'ahu) are visible even where the smooth interpolation surface cannot reach those peaks.

Island land boundaries are derived from the Hawaiʻi ahupuaʻa dataset, which provides more accurate coastlines than Natural Earth for all four islands (Natural Earth clips East Maui at the sample extent boundary). Small errant polygon fragments (< 1 km²) in the ahupuaʻa data are removed before computing the coastal band.

---

# Salinity-based enrichment above marine background

Within the same sampling event, sites with salinity above 34 PSU were minimally affected by freshwater runoff — they represent what the ocean chemistry looked like without the storm signal. Comparing these `r sum(chem$Salinity > 34, na.rm = TRUE)` "background" sites to the `r sum(chem$Salinity < 32, na.rm = TRUE)` most storm-influenced sites (Sal < 32 PSU) gives a direct, within-study measure of how much the storm changed things.

```{r}
#| label: salinity-baseline-enrichment
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "How much higher were nutrient levels in storm-influenced water compared to clean marine water sampled at the same time? (A) The fold-enrichment for each nutrient — how many times higher the typical storm-influenced concentration was relative to the marine background. Point size reflects the magnitude; error bars are 95% confidence intervals from 2,000 bootstrap resamples. SiO₂ was 6× higher, consistent with volcanic rock dissolving in freshwater and flowing into the coast. NO₃+NO₂ was 3× higher and PO₄ was about 2.3× higher, reflecting runoff from farms, cesspools, and soils. NH₃ was 2× higher but more variable, consistent with it coming partly from runoff and partly from biological processes. (B) The full distribution of concentrations in each zone. Dashed lines show the background zone means."

# ── Define salinity zones ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
sal_zones <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(Salinity)) |>
  mutate(zone = case_when(
    Salinity > 34.0 ~ "Background\n(Sal > 34 PSU)",
    Salinity < 32.0 ~ "Storm-influenced\n(Sal < 32 PSU)",
    TRUE            ~ NA_character_
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(zone))

bg   <- sal_zones |> filter(str_detect(zone, "Background"))
strm <- sal_zones |> filter(str_detect(zone, "Storm"))

nutrients_vec    <- c("NO3NO2", "PO4", "SiO2", "NH3")
nut_labels_ascii <- c("NO3+NO2", "PO4", "SiO2", "NH3")
zone_pal <- c(
  "Background\n(Sal > 34 PSU)"       = "#1565C0",
  "Storm-influenced\n(Sal < 32 PSU)" = "#E65100"
)

# ── Bootstrap fold-changes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
set.seed(4492)
ci_df <- map_dfr(seq_along(nutrients_vec), function(i) {
  nut  <- nutrients_vec[i]
  bg_v <- bg[[nut]];   bg_v <- bg_v[!is.na(bg_v)]
  st_v <- strm[[nut]]; st_v <- st_v[!is.na(st_v)]
  boot <- replicate(2000, {
    median(sample(st_v, replace = TRUE)) /
    median(sample(bg_v, replace = TRUE))
  })
  tibble(
    nutrient  = nut_labels_ascii[i],
    fold      = median(st_v) / median(bg_v),
    lo        = quantile(boot, 0.025),
    hi        = quantile(boot, 0.975)
  )
}) |>
  mutate(nutrient = factor(nutrient, levels = rev(nut_labels_ascii)))

# ── Panel A: fold-change ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pFold <- ggplot(ci_df, aes(x = fold, y = nutrient)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi),
                width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.6,
                color = "#37474F", orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(aes(size = fold), color = "#E65100", shape = 16) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(fold, 1), "\u00d7")),
            nudge_y = 0.38, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
            color = "#E65100") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 12), breaks = c(1, 2, 4, 8)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(3, 8), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x        = "Fold-enrichment  (storm-influenced \u00f7 background)",
    y        = NULL, tag = "A",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Background: Sal > 34 PSU (n = ", nrow(bg),
      ")  |  Storm-influenced: Sal < 32 PSU (n = ", nrow(strm), ")\n",
      "Error bars = 95% bootstrap CI on median ratio (2,000 replicates)"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor    = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y  = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold",
                                    family = "mono"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "gray40"),
        plot.tag      = element_text(face = "bold"))

# ── Panel B: distributions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
nut_long_zones <- sal_zones |>
  select(zone, all_of(nutrients_vec)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(nutrients_vec),
               names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc), conc > 0) |>
  mutate(
    nutrient = factor(recode(nutrient,
      "NO3NO2" = "NO3+NO2", "PO4" = "PO4",
      "SiO2"   = "SiO2",    "NH3" = "NH3"),
      levels = nut_labels_ascii),
    zone = factor(zone, levels = names(zone_pal))
  )

bg_means <- bg |>
  summarise(across(all_of(nutrients_vec), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "nutrient", values_to = "bg_mean") |>
  mutate(nutrient = factor(recode(nutrient,
    "NO3NO2" = "NO3+NO2", "PO4" = "PO4", "SiO2" = "SiO2", "NH3" = "NH3"),
    levels = nut_labels_ascii))

pDist <- ggplot(nut_long_zones,
                aes(x = zone, y = conc, fill = zone, color = zone)) +
  geom_hline(data = bg_means, aes(yintercept = bg_mean),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "gray30",
             linewidth = 0.5, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.30, linewidth = 0.3, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outliers = FALSE,
               fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = zone_pal) +
  scale_color_manual(values = zone_pal) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "\u03bcmol/L (log scale)", tag = "B") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor    = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x  = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 8),
        strip.text   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10.5,
                                    family = "mono"),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.tag     = element_text(face = "bold"))

pFold / pDist + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.1))
ggsave(here("output","nutrients_by_salinity.png"), width = 8, height = 6)
```

**Bottom line:** storm-influenced coastal water had silica levels 6× higher, nitrogen 3× higher, and phosphorus 2.3× higher than clean marine water sampled at the same time.

A second finding sits quietly in panel B: even the "background" high-salinity sites had notably elevated nitrogen and phosphorus compared to open-ocean values. Hawaiian coastal waters carry a persistent nutrient burden from cesspools and agriculture that exists year-round, independent of storms. The storm signal is piled on top of an already-elevated baseline — which makes the total impact even more concerning.

---

# Long-term baseline comparison: Hui o Ka Wai Ola monitoring data

The Hui o Ka Wai Ola programme has sampled fixed coastal stations in West and South Maui every month since 2016. Because we know what each site normally looks like, we can ask: how far outside the historical range did each site go during March 2026? This is a stronger test than comparing sites to each other — it uses each location as its own control.

**Units note:** Hui nutrients are reported in µg/L. Conversion to µmol/L: NNN ÷ 14.007 (as N); Phosphate ÷ 30.974 (as P); Silicate ÷ 28.086 (as Si).

```{r}
#| label: hui-baseline-fn
#| include: false

# Build a fold-change + forest-plot comparison for any Hui nutrient column.
#
# Args:
#   data      – bg_hui_loc (or any frame with Station, SiteName, region, Date,
#               and a pre-computed µmol/L column)
#   conc_col  – column name string, e.g. "NNN_umol", "Phosphate_umol"
#   x_label   – x-axis label for the forest plot panel

#   fold_text_cutoff – fold-change above which bar label flips white/inside

hui_baseline_plot <- function(data,
                              conc_col,
                              x_label,
                              fold_text_cutoff = 12,
                              cs_data          = NULL,
                              cs_radius        = 100) {

  # Map Hui µmol column names to the corresponding chem column
  cs_col_map <- c(NNN_umol       = "NO3NO2", Phosphate_umol = "PO4",
                  Silicate_umol  = "SiO2",   NH4_umol       = "NH3")
  cs_col  <- cs_col_map[conc_col]
  show_cs <- !is.null(cs_data) && !is.na(cs_col) && cs_col %in% names(cs_data)

  # ── Data prep ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  historical <- data |>
    filter(year(Date) < 2026, !is.na(.data[[conc_col]]))

  march <- data |>
    filter(year(Date) == 2026, month(Date) == 3) |>
    mutate(timing = if_else(Date < as.Date("2026-03-14"),
                            "Pre-storm (Mar 10)", "Post-storm (Mar 18\u201331)"))

  baselines <- historical |>
    group_by(Station, SiteName, region) |>
    summarise(
      p05 = quantile(.data[[conc_col]], 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
      p25 = quantile(.data[[conc_col]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      med = median(.data[[conc_col]],         na.rm = TRUE),
      p75 = quantile(.data[[conc_col]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      p95 = quantile(.data[[conc_col]], 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  post <- march |>
    filter(str_detect(timing, "Post"), !is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    left_join(baselines, by = c("Station", "SiteName", "region")) |>
    filter(!is.na(med)) |>
    mutate(
      conc        = .data[[conc_col]],
      fold_change = conc / med,
      above_p95   = conc > p95,
      label       = str_trunc(SiteName, 28, ellipsis = "\u2026"),
      region      = factor(region, levels = c("South Maui", "West Maui"))
    ) |>
    arrange(region, desc(fold_change))

  pre <- march |>
    filter(str_detect(timing, "Pre"), !is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    left_join(select(baselines, Station, SiteName, region, p05, p25, med, p75, p95),
              by = c("Station", "SiteName", "region")) |>
    mutate(
      conc   = .data[[conc_col]],
      label  = str_trunc(SiteName, 28, ellipsis = "\u2026"),
      region = factor(region, levels = c("South Maui", "West Maui"))
    )

  # Station order: most anomalous at top within each region
  lvls      <- post |> arrange(region, fold_change) |> pull(label)
  post      <- post      |> mutate(label = factor(label, levels = lvls))
  pre       <- pre       |> mutate(label = factor(label, levels = lvls))
  baselines <- baselines |>
    mutate(
      label  = factor(str_trunc(SiteName, 28, ellipsis = "\u2026"), levels = lvls),
      region = factor(region, levels = c("South Maui", "West Maui"))
    )

  # ── CS spatial match: mean of post-storm CS samples within cs_radius of each station
  if (show_cs) {
    hui_stations_sf <- data |>
      distinct(Station, SiteName, region, Lat, Long) |>
      filter(!is.na(Lat), !is.na(Long)) |>
      mutate(label = factor(str_trunc(SiteName, 28, ellipsis = "\u2026"), levels = lvls)) |>
      filter(!is.na(label)) |>
      sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("Long", "Lat"), crs = 4326) |>
      sf::st_transform(32604)

    cs_sf <- cs_data |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cs_col]]), .data[[cs_col]] > 0,
             !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
             as.Date(collected_hst, tz = "HST") >= as.Date("2026-03-14")) |>
      mutate(cs_val = .data[[cs_col]]) |>
      sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
      sf::st_transform(32604) |>
      dplyr::select(cs_val)

    cs_matched <- sf::st_join(
      hui_stations_sf, cs_sf,
      join = sf::st_is_within_distance, dist = cs_radius
    ) |>
      sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
      filter(!is.na(cs_val)) |>
      group_by(label, region) |>
      summarise(cs_val = mean(cs_val, na.rm = TRUE), n_cs = n(), .groups = "drop")
  }

  # ── Panel A: fold-change bars ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pA <- ggplot(post, aes(x = fold_change, y = label, fill = above_p95)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.65, color = NA) +
    geom_text(aes(label  = paste0(round(fold_change, 1), "\u00d7"),
                  hjust  = if_else(fold_change > fold_text_cutoff,  1.1, -0.1),
                  color  = if_else(fold_change > fold_text_cutoff, "white", "gray25")),
              size = 2.5, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#E65100", "FALSE" = "#90A4AE"),
                      labels = c("TRUE" = "Above 95th pct", "FALSE" = "Within range"),
                      name   = NULL) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22)),
                       breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 40)) +
    facet_grid(region ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    labs(x = "Fold above historical median", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      strip.placement    = "outside",
      legend.position    = "top",
      legend.text        = element_text(size = 8.5),
      axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 7, lineheight = 0.82),
      plot.tag           = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.caption       = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0)
    )

  # ── Panel B: build legend values conditionally on cs availability ─────────────
  legend_vals <- c("Historical median" = "white",
                   "Hui post-storm"    = "#E65100")
  legend_ov   <- list(size   = c(2,       3),
                      shape  = c(21,      21),
                      color  = c("gray40", "#B04000"),
                      stroke = c(0.5,     0.5),
                      alpha  = c(1,       0.95))
  if (show_cs && nrow(cs_matched) > 0) {
    legend_vals["Community science (≤100 m)"] <- "#AB47BC"
    legend_ov$size   <- c(legend_ov$size,   3)
    legend_ov$shape  <- c(legend_ov$shape,  21)
    legend_ov$color  <- c(legend_ov$color,  "#4A148C")
    legend_ov$stroke <- c(legend_ov$stroke, 1.2)
    legend_ov$alpha  <- c(legend_ov$alpha,  0.85)
  }

  # ── Panel B: forest plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  pB <- ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = filter(baselines, !is.na(label)),
                 aes(x = p05, xend = p95, y = label, yend = label),
                 color = "gray65", linewidth = 0.6, lineend = "round") +
    geom_segment(data = filter(baselines, !is.na(label)),
                 aes(x = p25, xend = p75, y = label, yend = label),
                 color = "gray30", linewidth = 3, lineend = "butt") +
    geom_point(data = filter(baselines, !is.na(label)),
               aes(x = med, y = label, fill = "Historical median"),
               color = "gray40", size = 1.8, shape = 21, stroke = 0.5) +
    (if (show_cs && nrow(cs_matched) > 0)
      geom_point(data = cs_matched,
                 aes(x = cs_val, y = label, fill = "Community science (≤100 m)"),
                 shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 1.2,
                 color = "#4A148C", alpha = 0.85)) +
    geom_point(data = filter(post, !is.na(label)),
               aes(x = conc, y = label, fill = "Hui post-storm"),
               color = "#B04000", shape = 21, size = 2, stroke = 0.5, alpha = 0.95) +
    scale_fill_manual(name   = NULL,
                      values = legend_vals,
                      guide  = guide_legend(override.aes = legend_ov)) +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = scales::breaks_log(n = 6),
                  labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.05))) +
    facet_grid(region ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      strip.text         = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y        = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y       = element_blank(),
      plot.tag           = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.margin        = margin(t = 4, r = 8, b = 4, l = 0),
      legend.position      = "bottom",
      legend.justification = "left",
      legend.text          = element_text(size = 7.5),
      legend.key.size      = unit(0.55, "lines")
    )

  # ── Assemble ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  (pA | pB) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, 1), guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      caption = "Source: Hui o Ka Wai Ola long-term monitoring programme (Falinski et al.)."
    ) &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = "center")
}
```

Orange bars = readings above that site's historical 95th percentile (i.e., higher than almost anything ever recorded there). Gray = within the normal historical range. ## Direct comparison: community science vs Hui within 100 m

To directly compare the two independent datasets at the same locations, we matched community science samples to Hui stations using a nearest-neighbour spatial join with a 100 m radius (UTM zone 4N). Both datasets are filtered to post-storm dates (≥ March 14, 2026). The datasets do not sample identically in time — Hui sampled March 18–31 and community science March 28–April 7 — so date difference (CS date − Hui date) is shown as point colour.

```{r}
#| label: hui-cs-comparison
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-cap: "Direct comparison of post-storm community science NO₃+NO₂ (y) against Hui o Ka Wai Ola NNN (x) at the same locations (within 100 m). Each point is one Hui station × CS sample pair. The dashed line is 1:1 agreement; colour shows the gap in days between the two sample dates (positive = CS collected after Hui). Only Maui stations are shown, as Hui monitoring is restricted to Maui."

# ── Hui post-storm: one row per station-date observation ─────────────────────
hui_match_sf <- bg_hui_loc |>
  filter(year(Date) == 2026, month(Date) == 3,
         Date >= as.Date("2026-03-14"),
         !is.na(Lat), !is.na(Long)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("Long", "Lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

# ── Post-storm community science samples (Maui only, with coordinates) ────────
cs_match_sf <- chem |>
  filter(island == "Maui",
         !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
         as.Date(collected_hst, tz = "HST") >= as.Date("2026-03-14")) |>
  mutate(cs_date = as.Date(collected_hst, tz = "HST")) |>
  select(sample_id, cs_date, cs_NO3NO2 = NO3NO2, cs_PO4 = PO4,
         cs_SiO2 = SiO2, cs_NH3 = NH3, latitude, longitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

# ── Spatial join: CS samples within 100 m of each Hui observation ─────────────
matched_pairs <- st_join(
  hui_match_sf,
  cs_match_sf,
  join    = st_is_within_distance,
  dist    = 100
) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(!is.na(sample_id)) |>
  mutate(
    date_diff = as.integer(cs_date - Date),  # positive = WIYW collected after Hui
    dist_label = "≤ 100 m"
  )

cat(glue::glue(
  "{nrow(matched_pairs)} Hui–CS pairs matched ",
  "({n_distinct(matched_pairs$Station)} Hui stations, ",
  "{n_distinct(matched_pairs$sample_id)} CS samples)\n",
  "Date gap range: {min(matched_pairs$date_diff)} to {max(matched_pairs$date_diff)} days\n"
))

# ── Reshape to long for faceting ──────────────────────────────────────────────
nutrient_map <- tribble(
  ~hui_col,        ~cs_col,      ~label,
  "NNN_umol",      "cs_NO3NO2",  "NO\u2083+NO\u2082",
  "Phosphate_umol","cs_PO4",     "PO\u2084",
  "Silicate_umol", "cs_SiO2",    "SiO\u2082",
  "NH4_umol",      "cs_NH3",     "NH\u2084"
)

pairs_long <- nutrient_map |>
  purrr::pmap(function(hui_col, cs_col, label) {
    matched_pairs |>
      filter(!is.na(.data[[hui_col]]), !is.na(.data[[cs_col]])) |>
      transmute(
        Station, SiteName, Date, cs_date, date_diff,
        hui_val = .data[[hui_col]],
        cs_val  = .data[[cs_col]],
        nutrient = label
      )
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(nutrient = factor(nutrient, levels = nutrient_map$label))

# ── Per-nutrient correlations for facet labels ────────────────────────────────
cor_labels <- pairs_long |>
  filter(hui_val > 0, cs_val > 0) |>
  group_by(nutrient) |>
  summarise(
    r   = cor(log10(hui_val), log10(cs_val), method = "pearson",  use = "complete.obs"),
    rho = cor(log10(hui_val), log10(cs_val), method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"),
    n   = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(
    nutrient, " (\u03bcmol/L)\n",
    "r = ", round(r, 2), "  \u03c1 = ", round(rho, 2), "  n = ", n
  ))

cor_labeller <- setNames(cor_labels$label, cor_labels$nutrient)

# ── Plot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ggplot(pairs_long |>
  filter(hui_val > 0, cs_val > 0), aes(x = hui_val, y = cs_val, color = date_diff)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0,
              linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_gradient2(
    low = "#1565C0", mid = "#FFA726", high = "#B71C1C", midpoint = 7,
    name = "Days WIYW\nafter Hui",
    guide = guide_colorbar(barheight = unit(8, "lines"), barwidth = unit(0.5, "lines"))
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~nutrient, scales = "free", ncol = 2,
             labeller = labeller(nutrient = cor_labeller)) +
  labs(
    x = "Hui o Ka Wai Ola (\u03bcmol/L, log)",
    y = "What's in your water (\u03bcmol/L, log)",
    caption = str_wrap("Direct comparison of post-storm WIYW community science NO₃+NO₂ (y) against Hui o Ka Wai Ola NNN (x) at the same locations (within 100 m). Each point is one Hui station × CS sample pair. The dashed line is 1:1 agreement; colour shows the gap in days between the two sample dates (positive = WIYW collected after Hui). Only Maui stations are shown, as Hui monitoring is restricted to Maui", width = 120)
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5),
    plot.caption       = element_text(size = 8, color = "gray50", hjust = 0)
  )
ggsave(here("output","comparisonHui_WIYW.png"))
```
