# Rainfall and coastal nutrients: 10 years of Hui o Ka Wai Ola

Hui monthly monitoring gives us a 10-year window to ask whether routine rainfall events drive coastal nutrient anomalies, or whether only extreme storms like the March 2026 Kona Low cross the threshold that matters for reef ecosystems. Using full-year monthly precipitation from CHIRPS (all 12 months, 2016–2026, fetched directly from the CHC server as cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs and cropped to the Maui island-mean bounding box), we compare rainfall against station-normalised nutrient fold-changes — how far each month's reading was above or below each station's own 10-year historical median.

```{r}
#| label: chirps-full-year-maui
#| include: false
#| cache: false
#
# Full-year CHIRPS monthly means for Maui, 2016–2026.
# Data source: CHIRPS v2.0 monthly COG product, Climate Hazards Center (CHC),
#   UC Santa Barbara. https://www.chc.ucsb.edu/data/chirps
# Citation: Funk et al. (2015) The climate hazards infrared precipitation
#   with stations — a new environmental record for monitoring extremes.
#   Scientific Data 2:150066. doi:10.1038/sdata.2015.66
#
# Method: terra::rast() via /vsicurl/ reads only the Hawaii bounding box
# from each global GeoTIFF without downloading the full file. Island-mean
# precipitation is computed as the mean of all non-fill pixels within
# lat 20.45–21.15, lon −156.75 to −155.9.

library(terra)

maui_ext <- ext(-156.75, -155.9, 20.45, 21.15)

fetch_chirps_month <- function(yr, mo) {
  url <- sprintf(
    "/vsicurl/https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS-2.0/global_monthly/cogs/chirps-v2.0.%04d.%02d.cog",
    yr, mo
  )
  tryCatch({
    r    <- rast(url) |> crop(maui_ext)
    vals <- as.vector(values(r))
    vals <- vals[vals > -9000 & !is.na(vals)]
    tibble(year=yr, month=mo, chirps_mm=mean(vals, na.rm=TRUE))
  }, error=function(e) tibble(year=yr, month=mo, chirps_mm=NA_real_))
}

chirps_full_cache <- here::here("data","chirps_maui_monthly_full.csv")

if (file.exists(chirps_full_cache)) {
  chirps_full_maui <- read_csv(chirps_full_cache, show_col_types=FALSE) |>
    mutate(ym = as.Date(paste(year, month, "1", sep="-")))
} else {
  yms <- expand_grid(year=2016:2026, month=1:12) |>
    filter(!(year==2026 & month > 7))
  chirps_full_maui <- map2_dfr(yms$year, yms$month, fetch_chirps_month) |>
    mutate(ym = as.Date(paste(year, month, "1", sep="-")))
  write_csv(chirps_full_maui, chirps_full_cache)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: hui-rainfall-nutrient
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "(A) CHIRPS island-mean monthly rainfall for Maui, 2016–2026, all 12 months. Dark blue bars = top 10% wettest months. March 2026 (373 mm) is 35% wetter than any prior month in the record. (B) Each point is one monthly Hui o Ka Wai Ola sampling event at all West and South Maui stations, showing median NO₃+NO₂ fold-change from each station's own historical baseline vs that month's CHIRPS rainfall (log scale). A statistically significant but modest log-linear relationship holds across the full decade (r² = 0.058, p = 0.009), confirming that wetter months produce proportionally elevated nitrogen. The March 2026 Kona Low sits far outside the envelope of any prior event — the only month to exceed 200 mm in the record and the only one to produce a >2× median fold-change."

# Station-level baselines (pre-2026)
station_baselines_hn <- bg_hui_loc |>
  filter(!is.na(NNN_umol), NNN_umol > 0, year(Date) < 2026) |>
  group_by(Station) |>
  summarise(hist_med_NNN  = median(NNN_umol,       na.rm=TRUE),
            hist_med_SiO2 = median(Silicate_umol,  na.rm=TRUE),
            hist_med_PO4  = median(Phosphate_umol, na.rm=TRUE),
            n_obs         = n(), .groups="drop") |>
  filter(n_obs >= 5)

# Monthly fold-change from station baseline
hui_anomaly_hn <- bg_hui_loc |>
  filter(!is.na(NNN_umol), NNN_umol > 0) |>
  inner_join(station_baselines_hn, by="Station") |>
  mutate(year  = year(Date),  month = month(Date),
         ym    = floor_date(Date,"month"),
         fold_NNN  = NNN_umol      / hist_med_NNN,
         fold_SiO2 = Silicate_umol / hist_med_SiO2,
         fold_PO4  = Phosphate_umol/ hist_med_PO4) |>
  group_by(ym, year, month) |>
  summarise(fold_NNN_med  = median(fold_NNN,  na.rm=TRUE),
            fold_SiO2_med = median(fold_SiO2, na.rm=TRUE),
            fold_PO4_med  = median(fold_PO4,  na.rm=TRUE),
            .groups="drop") |>
  left_join(chirps_full_maui |> select(ym, chirps_mm), by="ym")

# Model
lm_nnn_hn <- lm(fold_NNN_med ~ log1p(chirps_mm),
                 data=filter(hui_anomaly_hn, !is.na(chirps_mm)))
r2_hn <- round(summary(lm_nnn_hn)$r.squared, 3)
p_hn  <- round(summary(lm_nnn_hn)$coefficients[2,"Pr(>|t|)"], 4)

rain_q90 <- quantile(chirps_full_maui$chirps_mm, .90, na.rm=TRUE)

p_rain_hn <- ggplot(chirps_full_maui, aes(x=ym, y=chirps_mm)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill=chirps_mm >= rain_q90), width=25, show.legend=FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("FALSE"="#90CAF9","TRUE"="#1565C0")) +
  annotate("text", x=as.Date("2026-03-01"),
           y=max(chirps_full_maui$chirps_mm,na.rm=TRUE)*0.9,
           label="Mar 2026\n373 mm", size=2.8, color="#1565C0",
           hjust=0.5, fontface="italic", lineheight=0.85) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="1 year", date_labels="%Y") +
  labs(x=NULL, y="Rainfall (mm)", tag="A",
       subtitle=paste0("CHIRPS island-mean · all months 2016\u20132026  |  ",
                       "median ", round(median(chirps_full_maui$chirps_mm,na.rm=TRUE)),
                       " mm \u00b7 max 373 mm (Mar 2026)")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size=10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(), plot.tag=element_text(face="bold"),
        plot.subtitle=element_text(size=8, color="gray40"))

p_scatter_hn <- ggplot(
  hui_anomaly_hn |> filter(!is.na(chirps_mm)),
  aes(x=log1p(chirps_mm), y=fold_NNN_med)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype="dashed", color="gray60", linewidth=0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color=year>=2023), size=2.3, alpha=0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=TRUE, color="#E65100",
              fill="#FFE0CC", linewidth=0.9) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data=\(d) filter(d, year==2026, month==3),
    aes(label="Mar 2026\nKona Low"), size=2.6, color="#1565C0",
    lineheight=0.85, min.segment.length=0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("FALSE"="#90A4AE","TRUE"="#E65100"), guide="none") +
  annotate("text", x=3.2, y=max(hui_anomaly_hn$fold_NNN_med,na.rm=TRUE)*0.94,
           label=paste0("r\u00b2 = ",r2_hn,"\np = ",p_hn),
           size=2.9, color="#E65100", hjust=0, lineheight=1.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks=log1p(c(0,10,25,50,100,200,400)),
    labels=c("0","10","25","50","100","200","400")) +
  labs(x="Monthly rainfall, log scale (mm, CHIRPS island-mean)",
       y="NO\u2083+NO\u2082 fold-change\nfrom station baseline", tag="B",
       subtitle="Each point = one monthly Hui sampling  \u00b7  log scale removes right-skew") +
  theme_minimal(base_size=10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(), plot.tag=element_text(face="bold"),
        plot.subtitle=element_text(size=8, color="gray40"))

p_rain_hn / p_scatter_hn +
  plot_annotation(
    title="Maui coastal nitrogen responds to rainfall, but only extreme storms drive ecologically meaningful anomalies",
    subtitle="Hui o Ka Wai Ola fixed stations 2016\u20132026 \u00b7 station-normalised fold-change from 10-year baseline",
    theme=theme(plot.title=element_text(face="bold", size=11),
                plot.subtitle=element_text(size=8.5, color="gray40"))
  )
```

The log-linear relationship (r² = `r r2_hn`, p = `r p_hn`) confirms that monthly coastal nitrogen at Hui stations scales with antecedent rainfall, but the effect size is modest for routine events. The chronic nutrient load from cesspools and groundwater creates a persistently elevated baseline that obscures smaller storm signals at fixed leeward stations. Only the March 2026 Kona Low — with 373 mm, the wettest month in the 10-year record and 35% wetter than any previous event — produced a fold-change that clearly separates from this chronic background noise. This threshold behaviour is ecologically important: it means that routine Kona Low events may not substantially elevate nutrients above the already-elevated baseline at these semi-sheltered monitoring stations, while a single extreme event can deliver a nutrient pulse that is qualitatively different from anything observed in a decade of monthly monitoring.

---

# Stoichiometric fingerprints — Claim 2

Did all islands produce the same kind of runoff, or does each island have its own chemical identity? The ratios of nutrients to each other — nitrogen to phosphorus (N:P) and silica to nitrogen (Si:N) — act like a fingerprint that reveals where nutrients came from. Ocean plankton maintain nitrogen and phosphorus in a fairly fixed ratio of 16:1 (the Redfield ratio). Below 16 means unusual phosphorus enrichment, pointing to a cesspool or wastewater source. Above 1 for Si:N means silica-rich volcanic rock weathering is dominant. The four islands show distinctly different ratios, meaning the storm flushed island-specific chemical fingerprints — not a single uniform nutrient pulse.

```{r}
#| label: stoichiometry-figure
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Nitrogen-to-phosphorus ratio (N:P) by island. Ocean plankton normally maintain N:P near 16:1 (dashed line) — below 16 means there is more phosphorus than biology expects, pointing to wastewater or cesspool inputs. All four islands are below 16. (B) Silica-to-nitrogen ratio (Si:N). Values above 1 (dashed) indicate the water is carrying more dissolved rock material (silica from volcanic weathering) than nitrogen — the signature of storm runoff over Hawaiian terrain. (C) Both ratios together, with island medians shown as diamonds. All islands sit in the phosphorus-excess, silica-rich corner. Maui's ratio is closest to the biological reference line, suggesting its runoff has more agricultural nitrogen (which drives N:P up toward 16). Oʻahu and Molokaʻi are farther into the phosphorus-excess zone, consistent with denser cesspool infrastructure."


ratios <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(island), NO3NO2 > 0, PO4 > 0, SiO2 > 0) |>
  mutate(
    NP     = NO3NO2 / PO4,
    SiN    = SiO2   / NO3NO2,
    island = factor(island, levels = c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i", "Lāna'i"))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(island))

violin_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none")

pNP_s <- ggplot(ratios, aes(x = island, y = NP, fill = island, color = island)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 16, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 20, label = "Redfield N:P = 16",
           size = 2.7, color = "gray40", hjust = 1.05) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.30, linewidth = 0.35, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outliers = FALSE, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = island_pal) + scale_color_manual(values = island_pal) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(y = "N:P (molar, log)", tag = "A") + violin_theme

pSiN_s <- ggplot(ratios, aes(x = island, y = SiN, fill = island, color = island)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = 1.35, label = "Diatom Si:N = 1",
           size = 2.7, color = "gray40", hjust = 1.05) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.30, linewidth = 0.35, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outliers = FALSE, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = island_pal) + scale_color_manual(values = island_pal) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(y = "Si:N (molar, log)", tag = "B") + violin_theme

centroids_s <- ratios |>
  group_by(island) |>
  summarise(NP = median(NP, na.rm = TRUE), SiN = median(SiN, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

pScatter_s <- ggplot(ratios, aes(x = NP, y = SiN, color = island)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 16, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1,  linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.12, y = 0.13, label = "P-excess / Si-limited",
           size = 2.3, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 25,   y = 0.13, label = "N-excess / Si-limited",
           size = 2.3, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.12, y = 200,  label = "P-excess / Si-rich",
           size = 2.3, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 25,   y = 200,  label = "N-excess / Si-rich",
           size = 2.3, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = centroids_s, size = 5.5, shape = 18, alpha = 0.95) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = centroids_s, aes(label = island),
    size = 3, fontface = "bold", label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"),
    label.size = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000),
                labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = "N:P (molar, log)", y = "Si:N (molar, log)", tag = "C") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")

title_row_s <- ggdraw() +
  draw_label("Stoichiometric fingerprints distinguish island nutrient sources",
             fontface = "bold", size = 11, x = 0.01, hjust = 0) +
  draw_label("Dashed lines = Redfield N:P (16) and diatom Si:N (1). Diamonds = island medians.",
             color = "gray40", size = 9, x = 0.01, y = 0.2, hjust = 0)

plot_grid(
  title_row_s,
  plot_grid(pNP_s, pSiN_s, pScatter_s, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1, 1.4)),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.12, 1)
)
```

Maui's N:P ratio (median `r round(median(ratios$NP[ratios$island == "Maui"], na.rm=TRUE), 1)`) is noticeably higher than Oʻahu (`r round(median(ratios$NP[ratios$island == "O'ahu"], na.rm=TRUE), 1)`) and Molokaʻi (`r round(median(ratios$NP[ratios$island == "Moloka'i"], na.rm=TRUE), 1)`). That gap is consistent with East Maui's large farming areas contributing extra nitrogen — bumping the N:P ratio closer to the 16:1 biological baseline even while still remaining phosphorus-enriched. Every island has Si:N ratios well above 1, meaning volcanic rock dissolution is a dominant contributor across the board — an expected signature of Hawaiian watersheds. Each island's runoff tells a different story about its land use.

---

# Biogeochemical cluster analysis — Claims 2 & 4

We sorted the 694 sample sites into groups (using a statistical clustering method called PAM) based purely on their water chemistry: salinity, nitrogen, phosphorus, and silica. Four distinct water types emerged. The number four was chosen because it was the smallest number that captured all four clearly different kinds of coastal water without over-splitting into groups that were chemically too similar to distinguish. Testing two to six groups confirmed this choice.

```{r}
#| label: cluster-analysis
#| fig-height: 11
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "(A) Chemistry map of all 694 sites. The two axes (Principal Components) summarise the four measured variables: left-right roughly represents the land–sea gradient (right = cleaner ocean water, left = more land-influenced); up-down separates nitrogen-heavy from phosphorus-heavy enrichment. Coloured hulls enclose each of the four water types. (B) Chemical fingerprint for each group. Cell colours show whether a variable is above (red) or below (blue) the overall average — each water type has a distinct combination. Numbers are the actual median concentrations. (C) Which islands are in each group? Storm runoff sites are disproportionately Maui; marine background is dominated by Oʻahu. (D) Cesspool density in the watershed surrounding each site — runoff-affected groups sit in areas with more cesspool infrastructure. (E) Where on the map does each water type appear?"

# ── Prepare and cluster ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
chem_clust <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(island),
         !is.na(Salinity), !is.na(NO3NO2), !is.na(PO4), !is.na(SiO2)) |>
  mutate(log_NO3NO2 = log1p(NO3NO2),
         log_PO4    = log1p(PO4),
         log_SiO2   = log1p(SiO2))

clust_mat <- chem_clust |>
  select(Salinity, log_NO3NO2, log_PO4, log_SiO2) |>
  scale()

set.seed(8341)
pam4 <- pam(clust_mat, k = 4, pamonce = 5)

cluster_labels <- c("1" = "Marine background", "2" = "Storm runoff",
                    "3" = "Nearshore enriched",  "4" = "Freshwater plume")
cluster_pal_named <- c(
  "Marine background"  = "#1565C0", "Storm runoff"      = "#E65100",
  "Nearshore enriched" = "#2E7D32", "Freshwater plume"  = "#6A1B9A"
)

chem_clust <- chem_clust |>
  mutate(cluster       = factor(pam4$clustering),
         cluster_label = factor(cluster_labels[cluster],
                                levels = cluster_labels))

# ── PCA ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pca_res <- prcomp(clust_mat, scale. = FALSE)
pc_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2]) |>
  bind_cols(chem_clust |> select(cluster, cluster_label, island))
pct_var <- round(summary(pca_res)$importance[2, 1:2] * 100, 1)

loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_res$rotation[, 1:2]) |>
  rownames_to_column("variable") |>
  mutate(variable = recode(variable, "log_NO3NO2" = "NO3+NO2",
                           "log_PO4" = "PO4", "log_SiO2" = "SiO2"),
         scale = 3.2)

hulls <- pc_scores |>
  group_by(cluster_label) |>
  slice(chull(PC1, PC2))

pA_cl <- ggplot(pc_scores, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = cluster_label)) +
  geom_polygon(data = hulls, aes(fill = cluster_label),
               alpha = 0.08, linewidth = 0.3, color = NA) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(data = loadings,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1*scale, yend = PC2*scale),
               color = "gray25", linewidth = 0.6,
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.12, "inches"), type = "closed"),
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = loadings,
             aes(x = PC1*scale*1.15, y = PC2*scale*1.15, label = variable),
             size = 2.9, color = "gray20", linewidth = 0, fill = "white",
             fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal_named, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = cluster_pal_named, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pct_var[1], "% variance)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", pct_var[2], "% variance)"), tag = "A") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10.5) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "none",
        plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))

# ── Heatmap ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fp_vars   <- c("Salinity", "NO3NO2", "PO4", "SiO2")
fp_labels <- c("Salinity\n(PSU)", "NO3+NO2\n(µmol/L)", "PO4\n(µmol/L)", "SiO2\n(µmol/L)")

hm_df <- chem_clust |>
  group_by(cluster_label) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(fp_vars), ~median(., na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(-cluster_label, names_to = "variable", values_to = "median_val") |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  mutate(z = (median_val - mean(median_val)) / sd(median_val)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    variable      = factor(variable, levels = fp_vars, labels = fp_labels),
    cluster_label = factor(cluster_label, levels = rev(cluster_labels)),
    val_label     = case_when(
      variable == "Salinity\n(PSU)"    ~ as.character(round(median_val, 1)),
      variable == "NO3+NO2\n(µmol/L)" ~ as.character(round(median_val, 2)),
      variable == "PO4\n(µmol/L)"     ~ as.character(round(median_val, 3)),
      TRUE                             ~ as.character(round(median_val, 1))
    )
  )

pB_cl <- ggplot(hm_df, aes(x = variable, y = cluster_label, fill = z)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = val_label), size = 3, fontface = "bold",
            color = ifelse(abs(hm_df$z) > 1.2, "white", "gray20")) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1565C0", mid = "white", high = "#B71C1C",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "Z-score") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 14)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5), plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))

# ── Environmental drivers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# chem already carries ahupuaa / cesspool joins from the load-data chunk
env_df <- chem_clust

pC_cl <- env_df |>
  filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  count(cluster_label, island) |>
  group_by(cluster_label) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(island %in% c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i", "Lāna'i")) |>
  mutate(island = factor(island, levels = c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i", "Lāna'i"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cluster_label, y = pct, fill = island)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("O'ahu" = "#1565C0", "Maui" = "#2E7D32",
                               "Moloka'i" = "#E65100", "Lāna'i" = "#6A1B9A"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 10)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of sites", tag = "C") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right", plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))

pD_cl <- env_df |>
  filter(!is.na(cesspool_density_per_km2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cluster_label, y = cesspool_density_per_km2 + 0.01,
             fill = cluster_label, color = cluster_label)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.35, trim = TRUE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outliers = FALSE, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = cluster_pal_named) +
  scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal_named) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 10)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cesspool density\n(per km², log)", tag = "D") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none", plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"))

# ── Spatial maps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
clust_sf <- chem_clust |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

map_cluster_fn <- function(island_name, title = island_name) {
  match_idx <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_raw$mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)
  land_union <- ahupuaa_raw[match_idx, ] |>
    st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |> st_union()
  land_parts <- st_cast(land_union, "POLYGON")
  land_union  <- land_parts[as.numeric(st_area(land_parts)) > 1e6] |> st_union()
  coast_bbox  <- st_bbox(st_buffer(land_union, 3500))
  pts <- clust_sf |> filter(island == island_name)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = st_as_sf(st_sf(geometry = land_union)),
            fill = "gray78", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = pts, aes(color = cluster_label),
            size = ifelse(island_name == "O'ahu", 1.5, 2.2), alpha = 0.85, shape = 16) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal_named, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    coord_sf(crs = 32604, xlim = c(coast_bbox["xmin"], coast_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(coast_bbox["ymin"], coast_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 9) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2))
}

maps_row <- plot_grid(
  map_cluster_fn("O'ahu", "Oʻahu"), map_cluster_fn("Maui", "Maui"),
  map_cluster_fn("Moloka'i", "Molokaʻi"), map_cluster_fn("Lāna'i", "Lānaʻi"),
  nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1.6, 1.4, 0.9, 0.7)
)

# ── Assemble ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
legend_strip <- get_legend(
  pA_cl + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
                legend.key.size = unit(0.9, "lines"))
)

plot_grid(
  ggdraw() + draw_label(
    "Four biogeochemical clusters reveal distinct post-storm coastal water types",
    fontface = "bold", size = 11, x = 0.01, hjust = 0) +
    draw_label(
      paste0("PAM clustering on scaled log-nutrients + salinity (k = 4, n = ",
             nrow(chem_clust), " sites). Convex hulls in A = envelopes per cluster."),
      color = "gray40", size = 8.5, x = 0.01, y = 0.22, hjust = 0),
  plot_grid(
    plot_grid(pA_cl, pB_cl, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1.3, 1)),
    legend_strip,
    plot_grid(pC_cl, pD_cl, nrow = 1),
    ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.07, 0.75)
  ),
  plot_grid(
    ggdraw() + draw_label("Spatial distribution of biogeochemical clusters",
                          fontface = "bold", size = 9.5, x = 0.01, hjust = 0),
    maps_row, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1)
  ),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.06, 1.5, 0.65)
)
```

Four clearly distinct water types emerged from the grouping analysis. **Marine background** (n = `r sum(chem_clust$cluster == "1")`) is clean ocean water — high salinity, low nutrients — concentrated around Oʻahu's less impacted shores. **Storm runoff** (n = `r sum(chem_clust$cluster == "2")`) sites have extremely high nitrogen and silica with moderate freshwater dilution, the chemical signature of storm drainage carrying dissolved volcanic rock and soil nitrogen; most of these sites are on Maui's windward coast. **Nearshore enriched** (n = `r sum(chem_clust$cluster == "3")`) is the most common type — a broad mixing zone where nutrients are elevated but salinity hasn't dropped dramatically. **Freshwater plume** (n = `r sum(chem_clust$cluster == "4")`) sites sit right at stream mouths, with the lowest salinity (median 20.8 PSU) and extreme silica levels (median 48.1 µmol/L) — these are the most strongly land-influenced sites in the dataset. The areas with the most cesspools tend to have the most runoff-affected water types, indicating that wastewater infrastructure amplifies the nutrient signal beyond what natural soil flushing would produce alone.

Ammonium (NH₃) was not included in the grouping analysis. The figure below shows why: nitrogen (NO₃+NO₂) increases cleanly from marine background to freshwater plume, with almost no overlap between groups. NH₃, by contrast, is scattered across all four groups with overlapping ranges — it doesn't distinguish them. Adding it to the analysis weakened the group definitions (cluster quality dropped by 27%) and excluded 120 sites that lacked NH₃ measurements. NH₃ appears to build up through seafloor biological processes that are independent of storm runoff.

```{r}
#| label: nh3-posthoc
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "Why ammonium (NH₃) was left out of the grouping analysis. (A) NO₃+NO₂ by water type — each group is clearly separated from the others, with almost no overlap. This is what a useful grouping variable looks like. (B) NH₃ by water type — the distributions overlap substantially across all four groups. Including NH₃ would add noise, not clarity. NH₃ data available for `r sum(!is.na(chem_clust$NH3))` of `r nrow(chem_clust)` sites."

clust_pal_ch <- c(
  "Marine background"  = "#1565C0",
  "Storm runoff"       = "#E65100",
  "Nearshore enriched" = "#2E7D32",
  "Freshwater plume"   = "#6A1B9A"
)

vtheme_nh3 <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    axis.title.x       = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "gray40",
                                      margin = margin(t = 2, b = 4)),
    plot.tag           = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

nh3_df_ch <- chem_clust |>
  filter(!is.na(NH3), NH3 > 0) |>
```

# Supplementary: cluster selection rationale

```{r}
#| label: silhouette-supp
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "How was four groups chosen? (A) Silhouette width measures how well each site fits its assigned group versus how closely it matches neighbouring groups (higher = better-defined groups). Two groups scores highest, but splitting the coast into just 'freshwater' and 'marine' collapses the ecologically meaningful gradient into a binary that loses most of the information. Four groups (highlighted) is the smallest number that separates all four chemically distinct water types while still being well-defined. (B) Silhouette width for each of the 694 individual sites in the k = 4 solution. Negative values (sites that fit a neighbouring group slightly better) are concentrated at the Storm runoff / Nearshore enriched boundary — those two groups shade into each other chemically, which is ecologically expected for a continuous mixing gradient rather than a sharp boundary."

# clust_mat and pam4 are computed in the cluster-analysis chunk above
set.seed(8341)
sil_summary_s <- map_dfr(2:6, function(k) {
  pk  <- pam(clust_mat, k = k, pamonce = 5)
  sil <- silhouette(pk$clustering, dist(clust_mat))
  tibble(k = k, mean_sil = mean(sil[, 3]))
})

pSilA_s <- ggplot(sil_summary_s, aes(x = k, y = mean_sil)) +
  geom_line(color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, color = "gray30") +
  geom_point(data = filter(sil_summary_s, k == 4), size = 5.5, shape = 21,
             fill = "#E65100", color = "white", stroke = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.2, y = filter(sil_summary_s, k == 4)$mean_sil + 0.008,
           label = "k = 4\n(chosen)", hjust = 0, size = 3.2, color = "#E65100") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.18, 0.43)) +
  labs(x = "Number of clusters (k)", y = "Mean silhouette width",
       title = "A  Average silhouette width by k",
       subtitle = "Higher = more compact, better-separated clusters") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))

sil4_s <- as.data.frame(silhouette(pam4$clustering, dist(clust_mat))) |>
  mutate(
    cluster_label = factor(cluster_labels[cluster], levels = cluster_labels)
  ) |>
  arrange(cluster, sil_width) |>
  mutate(sorted_id = row_number())

pSilB_s <- ggplot(sil4_s, aes(x = sorted_id, y = sil_width, fill = cluster_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(sil4_s$sil_width),
             linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = nrow(sil4_s) * 0.98,
           y = mean(sil4_s$sil_width) + 0.03,
           label = sprintf("Mean = %.2f", mean(sil4_s$sil_width)),
           hjust = 1, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cluster_pal_named, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Sites (sorted within cluster)", y = "Silhouette width",
       title = "B  Individual silhouette widths, k = 4",
       subtitle = "Negative values = misclassified sites") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid  = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9), legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))

pSilA_s | pSilB_s
```

# Cluster–kriging overlay: where do fingerprints grade into hotspots?

The interpolated nitrogen map gives a continuous picture across the coast; the cluster labels give each site a chemical identity. Overlaying them shows whether the water types line up with the spatial hotspots — or whether the chemistry and geography tell different stories.

```{r}
#| label: krige-cluster-overlay
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "The nitrogen hotspot map with each sample's water type shown as a coloured circle. Background colour (yellow-green = high, dark purple = low) is the interpolated nitrogen map from community science samples. Circle colour shows which of the four water types that site belongs to. The two line up: clean marine-background sites (blue) sit in the dark, low-nitrogen margins; storm runoff (orange) and freshwater plume (purple) sites cluster in the brightest, highest-nitrogen patches, especially on Maui's north coast and Oʻahu's northwest shore. The transition group (nearshore enriched, green) forms a belt between the hotspot core and the clean outer water."

# krige_surface_data helper — same kriging logic as krige_island_map but
# returns components rather than a ggplot, allowing dual color scales.
krige_surface_data <- function(data, island_name, ahupuaa_sf,
                               res_m = 300, band_km = 3) {
  island_data <- data |>
    filter(island == island_name, !is.na(NO3NO2), !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude))
  match_idx  <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_sf$mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)
  land_union <- ahupuaa_sf[match_idx, ] |>
    st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |> st_union()
  land_parts <- st_cast(land_union, "POLYGON")
  land_union  <- land_parts[as.numeric(st_area(land_parts)) > 1e6] |> st_union()
  land_sf_out <- st_as_sf(st_sf(geometry = land_union))
  coast_outer <- st_buffer(land_union, dist = band_km * 1000)
  coast_band  <- st_difference(coast_outer, land_union)
  coast_bbox  <- st_bbox(coast_outer)
  pts_proj <- island_data |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604) |>
    mutate(log_val = log1p(NO3NO2),
           X = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], Y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
    group_by(X, Y) |>
    summarise(log_val = mean(log_val, na.rm = TRUE),
              NO3NO2  = mean(NO3NO2,  na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("X","Y"), crs = 32604)
  island_diag <- sqrt(diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")])^2 +
                      diff(st_bbox(pts_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")])^2)
  min_range <- island_diag / 5
  v_emp  <- variogram(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj)
  v_auto <- tryCatch(
    fit.variogram(v_emp, vgm(var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.8, "Sph",
                              min_range, var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.2)),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  v_fit <- if (!is.null(v_auto) && v_auto$range[2] >= min_range) v_auto else
    vgm(var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.8, "Sph", min_range, var(pts_proj$log_val)*0.2)
  sample_cov <- st_buffer(st_union(pts_proj), dist = min_range)
  grid_pts   <- st_make_grid(coast_band, cellsize = res_m, what = "centers") |>
    st_as_sf() |> st_filter(coast_band) |> st_filter(sample_cov)
  k_out   <- suppressWarnings(krige(log_val ~ 1, pts_proj, grid_pts,
                                     model = v_fit, nmax = 40))
  pred_df <- st_coordinates(k_out) |> as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(NO3NO2_pred = expm1(k_out$var1.pred))
  list(pred_df = pred_df, land_sf = land_sf_out, coast_bbox = coast_bbox)
}

# Attach cluster labels to chem (chem already has the chemistry needed for PAM)
chem_clust_overlay <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(Salinity), !is.na(NO3NO2), !is.na(PO4), !is.na(SiO2)) |>
  mutate(log_NO3NO2 = log1p(NO3NO2), log_PO4 = log1p(PO4), log_SiO2 = log1p(SiO2))

set.seed(8341)
pam4_ov <- pam(
  chem_clust_overlay |> select(Salinity, log_NO3NO2, log_PO4, log_SiO2) |> scale(),
  k = 4, pamonce = 5
)
chem_clust_overlay <- chem_clust_overlay |>
  mutate(cluster       = factor(pam4_ov$clustering),
         cluster_label = factor(cluster_labels[cluster], levels = cluster_labels))

krige_cluster_overlay_fn <- function(island_name, title = island_name, pt_size = 1.8) {
  kd  <- krige_surface_data(chem_clust_overlay, island_name, ahupuaa_raw)
  pts <- chem_clust_overlay |>
    filter(island == island_name, !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604)
  nice_cap <- ceiling(
    quantile(chem_clust_overlay$NO3NO2[chem_clust_overlay$island == island_name],
             0.95, na.rm = TRUE) / 5) * 5
  ggplot() +
    geom_raster(data = kd$pred_df, aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = NO3NO2_pred)) +
    geom_sf(data = kd$land_sf, fill = "gray72", color = "gray40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_sf(data = pts, aes(color = cluster_label),
            size = pt_size, alpha = 0.9, shape = 21, stroke = 0.9, fill = NA) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "NO3+NO2\n(umol/L)",
                         limits = c(0, nice_cap), oob = scales::squish,
                         labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal_named, name = "Cluster", guide = "none") +
    coord_sf(crs = 32604,
             xlim = c(kd$coast_bbox["xmin"], kd$coast_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(kd$coast_bbox["ymin"], kd$coast_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 9) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5, hjust = 0.5,
                                    margin = margin(b = 3)),
          legend.position    = "right",
          legend.title       = element_text(size = 7.5),
          legend.text        = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.key.height  = unit(1.6, "lines"))
}

p_ov_oahu    <- krige_cluster_overlay_fn("O'ahu",    "Oʻahu",    pt_size = 1.4)
p_ov_maui    <- krige_cluster_overlay_fn("Maui",     "Maui",     pt_size = 2.0)
p_ov_molokai <- krige_cluster_overlay_fn("Moloka'i", "Molokaʻi", pt_size = 2.2)

cl_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(

    geom_point(size = 3.5, shape = 21, stroke = 1.2, fill = NA) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cluster_pal_named, name = "Cluster") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
          legend.text  = element_text(size = 8.5),
          legend.key.size = unit(1, "lines"))
)

fill_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(
  p_ov_oahu + theme(legend.position = "bottom",
                    legend.title = element_text(size = 8.5),
                    legend.text  = element_text(size = 8),
                    legend.key.width = unit(2, "lines"))
)

cowplot::plot_grid(
  cowplot::plot_grid(
    p_ov_oahu    + theme(legend.position = "none"),
    p_ov_maui    + theme(legend.position = "none"),
    p_ov_molokai + theme(legend.position = "none"),
    nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1.6, 1.4, 0.9), align = "h"
  ),
  cowplot::plot_grid(fill_legend, cl_legend, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1.4)),
  ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.2)
)
```

# Random forest: landscape predictors of cluster membership — Claim 4

Can we predict which type of water a site will have — before any sampling — just from publicly available maps and records? We used a random forest model (an ensemble of 1,000 decision trees) with thirteen landscape and hydrological predictors. **Infrastructure proximity**: distance to the nearest cesspool, cesspool density per ahupuaʻa, and distance to the nearest NPDES discharge point (wastewater treatment plant outfall or industrial discharge; EPA ECHO 2025). **Storm delivery**: distance to the nearest stream mouth (OpenStreetMap), mean daily discharge in March 2026 from the nearest USGS gauge within 15 km. **Land cover**: % impervious surface and % agricultural land (NOAA C-CAP 2010–2011). **Watershed hydrology**: mean slope per ahupuaʻa (NASA SRTM via *elevatr*; Farr et al. 2007) and soil saturated hydraulic conductivity (SSURGO Ksat, top 100 cm; USDA NRCS 2024) — which together control how fast rainfall becomes runoff. **Pre-storm conditions**: root-zone soil wetness in the 30 days before the storm (NASA POWER, Feb 1–Mar 10 2026; Sparks et al. 2018). **Livestock density**: cattle per km² of agricultural land (USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture). **Island identity**. Latitude and longitude were excluded so the model reflects real landscape drivers rather than geography.

```{r}
#| label: stream-mouths-cache
#| include: false

cache_path <- here::here("data", "osm_stream_mouths.csv")

if (file.exists(cache_path)) {

  stream_mouths_sf <- read_csv(cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    sf::st_transform(32604)

} else {

  island_bbs <- list(
    "O'ahu"    = c(-158.32, 21.22, -157.60, 21.73),
    "Maui"     = c(-156.70, 20.50, -155.94, 21.05),
    "Moloka'i" = c(-157.37, 21.04, -156.70, 21.24),
    "Lāna'i"   = c(-157.08, 20.71, -156.83, 20.95)
  )

  fetch_endpoints <- function(bb, island_name) {
    message("Fetching waterways: ", island_name)
    osm <- tryCatch(
      opq(bbox = bb, timeout = 120) |>
        add_osm_feature(key = "waterway", value = c("river", "stream")) |>
        osmdata_sf(),
      error = function(e) { warning(island_name, ": ", e$message); NULL }
    )
    lines <- osm$osm_lines
    if (is.null(lines) || nrow(lines) == 0) return(NULL)

    ep_list <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(lines)), function(i) {
      coords <- st_coordinates(lines[i, ])
      data.frame(lon = c(coords[1, "X"], coords[nrow(coords), "X"]),
                 lat = c(coords[1, "Y"], coords[nrow(coords), "Y"]))
    })
    bind_rows(ep_list) |>
      st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
      st_transform(32604) |>
      mutate(island = island_name)
  }

  all_endpoints <- map2(island_bbs, names(island_bbs), fetch_endpoints) |>
    compact() |>
    bind_rows()

  # Filter to endpoints within 400 m of the coastline
  coastlines_sm <- map(names(island_bbs), function(isl) {
    norm <- normalize_name(isl)
    idx  <- normalize_name(ahupuaa_raw$mokupuni) == norm
    ahupuaa_raw[idx, ] |>
      st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |> st_union() |>
      st_cast("POLYGON") |>
      (\(p) p[as.numeric(st_area(p)) > 1e6])() |>
      st_union() |>
      st_boundary()
  }) |> setNames(names(island_bbs))

  mouth_list <- map(names(island_bbs), function(isl) {
    pts   <- all_endpoints |> filter(island == isl)
    coast <- coastlines_sm[[isl]]
    pts[as.numeric(st_distance(pts, coast)) <= 400, ]
  })

  stream_mouths_sf <- bind_rows(mouth_list)
  stream_mouths_sf |>
    sf::st_transform(4326) |>    # save as WGS84 degrees, not UTM metres
    dplyr::mutate(longitude = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
                  latitude  = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,2]) |>
    sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
    readr::write_csv(cache_path)
  message("Stream mouths fetched and cached: ", nrow(stream_mouths_sf), " candidates")

}

# Compute distance from every chem site with coordinates to nearest stream mouth
chem_sf_rf <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(chem_sf_rf, stream_mouths_sf)
chem_with_stream <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude)) |>
  mutate(dist_to_stream_mouth_m = as.numeric(
    st_distance(chem_sf_rf, stream_mouths_sf[nearest_idx, ], by_element = TRUE)
  ))
```

```{r}
#| label: ccap-landcover-cache
#| include: false

ccap_cache_path <- here::here("data", "ccap_ahupuaa_summary.csv")

if (file.exists(ccap_cache_path)) {

  ccap_summary <- read_csv(ccap_cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

} else {

  ccap_base_url <- "https://chs.coast.noaa.gov/htdata/raster1/landcover/bulkdownload/hires/hi/"
  ccap_files <- c(
    "O'ahu"    = "hi_oahu_2011_ccap_hr_land_cover20140619.img",
    "Maui"     = "hi_maui_2010_ccap_hr_land_cover_20150213.img",
    "Moloka'i" = "hi_molokai_2010_ccap_hr_land_cover20150102.img",
    "Lāna'i"   = "hi_lanai_2011_ccap_hr_land_cover_20141204.img"
  )

  dir.create(here::here("data", "ccap"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (isl in names(ccap_files)) {
    dest <- here::here("data", "ccap", ccap_files[isl])
    if (!file.exists(dest))
      download.file(paste0(ccap_base_url, ccap_files[isl]), dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  }

  # C-CAP class groups: impervious = high/med/low developed; agriculture = cultivated + pasture
  IMPERVIOUS  <- c(2, 3, 4)
  AGRICULTURE <- c(6, 7)

  summarise_ccap <- function(island_name, img_file) {
    r   <- rast(here::here("data", "ccap", img_file))
    ahu <- ahupuaa_raw |>
      filter(normalize_name(mokupuni) == normalize_name(island_name)) |>
      st_transform(crs(r)) |>
      st_make_valid()
    fracs   <- exact_extract(r, ahu, "frac", progress = FALSE)
    imp_cols <- paste0("frac_", IMPERVIOUS)
    agr_cols <- paste0("frac_", AGRICULTURE)
    ahu |>
      st_drop_geometry() |>
      select(ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni) |>
      mutate(
        island          = island_name,
        pct_impervious  = rowSums(fracs[, intersect(imp_cols, names(fracs)), drop=FALSE], na.rm=TRUE),
        pct_agriculture = rowSums(fracs[, intersect(agr_cols, names(fracs)), drop=FALSE], na.rm=TRUE)
      )
  }

  ccap_summary <- map2(names(ccap_files), ccap_files, summarise_ccap) |> bind_rows()
  write_csv(ccap_summary, ccap_cache_path)

}
```

```{r}
#| label: additional-predictors-cache
#| include: false
#
# Six additional landscape predictors joined to the RF dataset.
# Each is cached to data/ on first run; subsequent renders read from cache.
#
# CITATIONS
# Watershed slope: NASA SRTM v3 (Farr et al. 2007, Rev. Geophys.); accessed
#   via elevatr R package (Hollister et al. 2023, JOSS).
# Soil permeability: USDA SSURGO (Soil Survey Staff, NRCS, USDA 2024); queried
#   via soilDB Soil Data Access API (Beaudette et al. 2022, Comput. Geosci.).
#   Ksat = saturated hydraulic conductivity (µm/s), mean over top 100 cm per
#   ahupuaʻa centroid.
# NPDES outfall distance: US EPA ICIS-NPDES Discharge Points national layer
#   (US EPA ECHO 2025; echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/npdes_outfalls_layer.zip).
#   Distance to nearest permitted discharge point (WWTPs, ocean outfalls,
#   industrial stormwater, injection wells).
# Antecedent soil moisture: NASA POWER (Sparks et al. 2018, AAAS);
#   GWETROOT = root-zone soil wetness fraction, 0.5° grid, mean Feb 1–Mar 10 2026
#   (30-day pre-storm window). Retrieved via nasapower R package (Sparks 2023).
# Livestock density: USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture (USDA NASS 2024);
#   cattle & calves inventory per km² of agricultural land, by county.
#   Maui County covers Maui, Molokaʻi, and Lānaʻi; Honolulu County = Oʻahu.
# Soil permeability method: for each ahupuaʻa centroid (WGS84), SDA_query() was
#   used to identify the dominant soil map unit and compute mean Ksat from all
#   horizons in the top 100 cm with reported values (SSURGO tabular data via SDA).

# ── 1. Watershed slope ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
slope_cache <- here::here("data", "ahupuaa_slope.csv")
if (!file.exists(slope_cache)) {
  islands_needed <- c("O'ahu","Maui","Moloka'i","L\u0101na'i")
  slope_by_island <- purrr::map(islands_needed, function(isl) {
    ahu_isl <- ahupuaa_raw |>
      filter(normalize_name(mokupuni) == normalize_name(isl)) |>
      st_make_valid()
    elev    <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(ahu_isl, z = 10, clip = "locations",
                                        src = "aws", verbose = FALSE) |>
      terra::rast() |> terra::project("EPSG:32604")
    slope_r <- terra::terrain(elev, v = "slope", unit = "degrees")
    ahu_proj <- ahu_isl |> st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid()
    exactextractr::exact_extract(slope_r, ahu_proj, "mean", progress=FALSE) |>
      tibble::tibble(mean_slope_deg = _) |>
      dplyr::bind_cols(ahu_proj |> st_drop_geometry() |>
                         dplyr::select(ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(island = isl)
  })
  slope_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(slope_by_island)
  write_csv(slope_df, slope_cache)
} else { slope_df <- read_csv(slope_cache, show_col_types = FALSE) }

# ── 2. Soil permeability (SSURGO Ksat) ────────────────────────────────────
ksat_cache <- here::here("data", "ahupuaa_ksat.csv")
if (!file.exists(ksat_cache)) {
  ksat_raw <- soilDB::SDA_query(
    "SELECT mu.mukey, AVG(ch.ksat_r) AS mean_ksat_um_s
     FROM mapunit mu
     JOIN component co ON mu.mukey=co.mukey AND co.majcompflag='Yes'
     JOIN chorizon ch  ON co.cokey=ch.cokey
     JOIN legend   le  ON mu.lkey=le.lkey
     WHERE le.areasymbol LIKE 'HI%'
       AND ch.hzdept_r < 100 AND ch.ksat_r IS NOT NULL
     GROUP BY mu.mukey"
  )
  ahu_centroids_sda <- ahupuaa_raw |>
    filter(normalize_name(mokupuni) %in%
             normalize_name(c("O'ahu","Maui","Moloka'i","L\u0101na'i"))) |>
    st_centroid() |> st_transform(4326) |>
    mutate(lon = st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
           lat = st_coordinates(geometry)[,2]) |>
    st_drop_geometry()
  get_ksat_pt <- function(lon, lat) {
    q <- sprintf(
      "SELECT mu.mukey, AVG(ch.ksat_r) AS mean_ksat
       FROM mapunit mu JOIN component co ON mu.mukey=co.mukey AND co.majcompflag='Yes'
       JOIN chorizon ch ON co.cokey=ch.cokey
       WHERE mu.mukey IN (SELECT mukey FROM
         SDA_Get_Mukey_from_intersection_with_WktWgs84('POINT(%s %s)'))
         AND ch.hzdept_r < 100 AND ch.ksat_r IS NOT NULL GROUP BY mu.mukey",
      round(lon,6), round(lat,6))
    res <- tryCatch(soilDB::SDA_query(q), error=function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(res)||nrow(res)==0) NA_real_ else mean(res$mean_ksat, na.rm=TRUE)
  }
  ksat_df <- ahu_centroids_sda |>
    dplyr::mutate(mean_ksat_um_s = purrr::map2_dbl(lon, lat, get_ksat_pt)) |>
    dplyr::select(ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni, mean_ksat_um_s)
  write_csv(ksat_df, ksat_cache)
} else { ksat_df <- read_csv(ksat_cache, show_col_types = FALSE) }

# ── 3. NPDES outfall / WWTP locations ─────────────────────────────────────
echo_cache <- here::here("data", "epa_facilities_hi.csv")
if (!file.exists(echo_cache)) {
  tmp_zip <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  tmp_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "npdes_outfalls")
  dir.create(tmp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  download.file("https://echo.epa.gov/files/echodownloads/npdes_outfalls_layer.zip",
                tmp_zip, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  unzip(tmp_zip, exdir = tmp_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  outfalls_raw <- readr::read_csv(
    file.path(tmp_dir, "npdes_outfalls_layer.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  outfalls_hi <- outfalls_raw |>
    dplyr::filter(STATE_CODE == "HI", !is.na(LATITUDE83), !is.na(LONGITUDE83),
                  LATITUDE83 > 18, LATITUDE83 < 23) |>
    dplyr::transmute(facility_name = FACILITY_NAME,
                     lat = LATITUDE83, lon = LONGITUDE83)
  write_csv(outfalls_hi, echo_cache)
} else { outfalls_hi <- read_csv(echo_cache, show_col_types = FALSE) }

outfalls_sf <- outfalls_hi |>
  dplyr::distinct(facility_name, lat, lon) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_transform(32604)

# ── 4. Antecedent soil moisture (NASA POWER) ──────────────────────────────
smap_cache <- here::here("data", "nasa_power_soilmoist.csv")
if (!file.exists(smap_cache)) {
  island_pts <- tibble::tribble(
    ~island,    ~lon,      ~lat,
    "O'ahu",   -157.98,   21.47,
    "Maui",    -156.34,   20.80,
    "Moloka'i",-157.02,   21.13,
    "L\u0101na'i", -156.92, 20.83
  )
  sm_df <- purrr::pmap_dfr(island_pts, function(island, lon, lat) {
    nasapower::get_power(community="ag", lonlat=c(lon,lat),
                         pars="GWETROOT",
                         dates=c("2026-02-01","2026-03-10"),
                         temporal_api="daily") |>
      dplyr::summarise(mean_gwetroot = mean(GWETROOT, na.rm=TRUE)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(island = island)
  })
  write_csv(sm_df, smap_cache)
} else { sm_df <- read_csv(smap_cache, show_col_types = FALSE) }
sm_df <- sm_df |>
  mutate(island = stringr::str_replace_all(island, "[\u02BB\u02BC\u2018\u2019]", "'"))

# ── 5. Livestock density (USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture) ───────────
livestock_cache <- here::here("data", "usda_nass_livestock_hi.csv")
if (!file.exists(livestock_cache)) {
  # Cattle & calves inventory and agricultural land by county
  # Source: USDA NASS 2022 Census of Agriculture, Table 11 (published Feb 2024)
  livestock_by_island <- tibble::tribble(

    "Maui",     56.1,   # Maui County (Maui+Molokai+Lanai): 35,741 / 636.8 km²
    "Moloka'i", 56.1,
    "L\u0101na'i", 56.1
  )

} else { livestock_by_island <- read_csv(livestock_cache, show_col_types = FALSE) }
livestock_by_island <- livestock_by_island |>
  mutate(island = stringr::str_replace_all(island, "[\u02BB\u02BC\u2018\u2019]", "'"))

# ── Join all new predictors to chem_with_discharge ────────────────────────
island_norm <- c("oahu"="O'ahu","maui"="Maui","molokai"="Moloka'i",
                 "lanai"="L\u0101na'i")

add_island_col <- function(df) {
  df |> dplyr::mutate(island = island_norm[normalize_name(mokupuni)])
}

slope_j <- slope_df |> add_island_col() |> filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, island) |>
  summarise(mean_slope_deg = mean(mean_slope_deg, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop")

ksat_j <- ksat_df |> add_island_col() |> filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  group_by(ahupuaa, island) |>
  summarise(mean_ksat_um_s = mean(mean_ksat_um_s, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop")

sm_j <- sm_df |> dplyr::select(island, mean_gwetroot)
lv_j <- livestock_by_island |> dplyr::select(island, cattle_per_km2)
```

```{r}
#| label: usgs-discharge-cache
#| include: false

discharge_cache <- here::here("data", "usgs_discharge_march2026.csv")
gauge_cache     <- here::here("data", "usgs_gauges_march2026.csv")

if (file.exists(discharge_cache) && file.exists(gauge_cache)) {

  discharge_per_ahu <- read_csv(discharge_cache, show_col_types = FALSE,
                                col_types = cols(site_no = col_character()))
  gauge_sf <- read_csv(gauge_cache, show_col_types = FALSE,
                       col_types = cols(site_no = col_character())) |>
    sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
    sf::st_transform(32604)

} else {

  hi_sites <- dataRetrieval::whatNWISsites(
    stateCd = "HI", siteType = "ST",
    parameterCd = "00060", hasDataTypeCd = "dv"
  )

  site_batches <- split(hi_sites$site_no,
                        ceiling(seq_along(hi_sites$site_no) / 100))

  discharge_raw <- purrr::map_dfr(site_batches, function(sites) {
    tryCatch(
      dataRetrieval::readNWISdv(
        siteNumbers = sites, parameterCd = "00060",
        startDate = "2026-03-01", endDate = "2026-03-31"
      ) |> dataRetrieval::renameNWISColumns(),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
  })

  march_discharge <- discharge_raw |>
    filter(!is.na(Flow), Flow >= 0) |>
    group_by(site_no) |>
    summarise(mean_cfs_march = mean(Flow, na.rm = TRUE),
              n_days         = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    filter(n_days >= 15)

  gauge_sf <- hi_sites |>
    select(site_no, station_nm, dec_lat_va, dec_long_va) |>
    filter(!is.na(dec_lat_va), !is.na(dec_long_va)) |>
    inner_join(march_discharge, by = "site_no") |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("dec_long_va", "dec_lat_va"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(32604)

  gauge_ahu <- st_join(
    gauge_sf,
    ahupuaa_raw |> st_transform(32604) |> st_make_valid() |>
      select(ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni),
    join = st_within
  ) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(!is.na(ahupuaa))

  discharge_per_ahu <- gauge_ahu |>
    group_by(ahupuaa, moku, mokupuni) |>
    summarise(total_cfs_march = sum(mean_cfs_march),
              n_gauges        = n(), .groups = "drop")

  write_csv(discharge_per_ahu, discharge_cache)
  gauge_sf |>
    sf::st_transform(4326) |>    # save as WGS84 degrees, not UTM metres
    dplyr::mutate(longitude = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
                  latitude  = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,2]) |>
    sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
    readr::write_csv(gauge_cache)
  message("Discharge cached: ", nrow(gauge_sf), " gauges, ",
          nrow(discharge_per_ahu), " ahupuaa")
}

# Assign nearest gauge discharge to each chem site (within 15 km)
chem_sf_discharge <- chem_with_stream |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
         !is.na(Salinity), !is.na(NO3NO2), !is.na(PO4), !is.na(SiO2)) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(32604)

nearest_idx  <- st_nearest_feature(chem_sf_discharge, gauge_sf)
nearest_dist <- as.numeric(st_distance(chem_sf_discharge,
                                        gauge_sf[nearest_idx, ],
                                        by_element = TRUE))

chem_with_discharge <- chem_with_stream |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
         !is.na(Salinity), !is.na(NO3NO2), !is.na(PO4), !is.na(SiO2)) |>
  mutate(
    mean_cfs_march    = if_else(nearest_dist > 15000, NA_real_,
                                gauge_sf$mean_cfs_march[nearest_idx]),
    log_discharge_cfs = log1p(mean_cfs_march)
  )

# Compute distance from each chem site to nearest NPDES outfall
# (outfalls_sf is created in additional-predictors-cache above)
chem_sf_out    <- chem_with_discharge |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude","latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_transform(32604)

outfall_nn_idx <- sf::st_nearest_feature(chem_sf_out, outfalls_sf)
outfall_dist_v <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(chem_sf_out,
                                              outfalls_sf[outfall_nn_idx, ],
                                              by_element = TRUE))

chem_enhanced_base <- chem_with_discharge |>
  mutate(log_dist_outfall = log1p(outfall_dist_v))
```

```{r}
#| label: random-forest-cluster
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Which landscape features matter most for predicting water type? Bar length = variable importance (how much accuracy drops when that variable's values are shuffled randomly). March stream discharge (mean daily flow in cubic feet per second from the nearest USGS gauge within 15 km) is the third strongest predictor — behind stream mouth proximity and cesspool proximity, but ahead of land cover. Discharge captures how much water actually flowed during the storm, adding information beyond just knowing where streams are. (B) How often did the model get each water type right? Rows = actual water type; columns = predicted; numbers = % of each row. The model is most accurate for marine background and freshwater plume, and most confused at the storm runoff / nearshore enriched boundary."

# Build cluster assignments; join stream mouth distances from chem_with_stream
chem_rf_base <- chem_enhanced_base |>
  mutate(log_NO3NO2 = log1p(NO3NO2), log_PO4 = log1p(PO4), log_SiO2 = log1p(SiO2))

set.seed(8341)
pam_rf <- pam(
  chem_rf_base |> select(Salinity, log_NO3NO2, log_PO4, log_SiO2) |> scale(),
  k = 4, pamonce = 5
)

rf_base_joined <- chem_rf_base |>
  mutate(cluster       = factor(pam_rf$clustering),
         cluster_label = factor(cluster_labels[cluster], levels = cluster_labels)) |>
  left_join(
    ccap_summary |>
      group_by(ahupuaa, island) |>
      summarise(pct_impervious  = mean(pct_impervious,  na.rm = TRUE),
                pct_agriculture = mean(pct_agriculture, na.rm = TRUE),
                .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("ahupuaa", "island")
  ) |>
  left_join(slope_j, by = c("ahupuaa","island"), relationship="many-to-one") |>
  left_join(ksat_j,  by = c("ahupuaa","island"), relationship="many-to-one") |>
  left_join(sm_j,   by = "island") |>
  left_join(lv_j,   by = "island")

rf_df_qmd <- rf_base_joined |>
  filter(!is.na(cesspool_density_per_km2),
         !is.na(dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m),
         !is.na(dist_to_stream_mouth_m),
         !is.na(pct_impervious),
         !is.na(log_discharge_cfs)) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(mean_slope_deg, mean_ksat_um_s, log_dist_outfall,
             mean_gwetroot, cattle_per_km2),
           \(x) if_else(is.na(x), median(x, na.rm = TRUE), x))
  ) |>
  transmute(
    cluster_label,
    island                = factor(island),
    log_cesspool_density  = log1p(cesspool_density_per_km2),
    log_dist_cesspool     = log1p(dist_to_nearest_cesspool_m),
    log_dist_stream_mouth = log1p(dist_to_stream_mouth_m),
    log_discharge_cfs,
    pct_impervious,
    pct_agriculture,
    mean_slope_deg,
    log_ksat              = log1p(mean_ksat_um_s),
    log_dist_outfall,
    mean_gwetroot,
    log_cattle_km2        = log1p(cattle_per_km2)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(cluster_label), !is.na(log_cesspool_density),
         !is.na(log_dist_cesspool), !is.na(log_dist_stream_mouth),
         !is.na(pct_impervious), !is.na(pct_agriculture))

set.seed(5572)
rf_fit_qmd <- ranger(
  cluster_label ~ .,
  data      = rf_df_qmd,
  num.trees = 1000,
  mtry      = 4,
  importance = "permutation",
  seed      = 5572
)

oob_acc  <- round((1 - rf_fit_qmd$prediction.error) * 100, 1)
null_acc <- round(max(table(rf_df_qmd$cluster_label)) / nrow(rf_df_qmd) * 100, 1)

# Variable importance
imp_df_qmd <- enframe(rf_fit_qmd$variable.importance,
                       name = "predictor", value = "importance") |>
  mutate(
    predictor = recode(predictor,
      "log_cesspool_density"  = "Cesspool density\n(ahupuaʻa, log)",
      "log_dist_cesspool"     = "Dist. to nearest\ncesspool (log m)",
      "log_dist_stream_mouth" = "Dist. to nearest\nstream mouth (log m)",
      "log_discharge_cfs"     = "March discharge\n(log cfs)",
      "pct_impervious"        = "% Impervious surface\n(C-CAP)",
      "pct_agriculture"       = "% Agriculture\n(C-CAP)",
      "mean_slope_deg"        = "Watershed slope\n(SRTM, deg)",
      "log_ksat"              = "Soil permeability\n(SSURGO Ksat, log µm/s)",
      "log_dist_outfall"      = "Dist. to nearest\nNPDES outfall (log m)",
      "mean_gwetroot"         = "Pre-storm soil moisture\n(NASA POWER, Feb–Mar10)",
      "log_cattle_km2"        = "Livestock density\n(NASS 2022, log head/km²)",
      "island"                = "Island"
    ),
    importance = importance / max(importance)
  )

pImp_qmd <- ggplot(imp_df_qmd, aes(x = importance,
                                    y = reorder(predictor, importance))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#37474F", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(importance, 2)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.15), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Relative importance (Gini impurity, normalised)", y = NULL,
       title = "A  Variable importance",
       subtitle = sprintf("OOB accuracy = %.1f%%  (null = %.1f%%)",
                          oob_acc, null_acc)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))

# Confusion matrix
conf_df_qmd <- as.data.frame(rf_fit_qmd$confusion.matrix) |>
  rename(true_label = true, n = Freq) |>
  group_by(true_label) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n),
         true_label = factor(true_label, levels = rev(cluster_labels)),
         predicted  = factor(predicted,  levels = cluster_labels)) |>
  ungroup()

pConf_qmd <- ggplot(conf_df_qmd, aes(x = predicted, y = true_label, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, sprintf("%d\n%.0f%%", n, pct * 100), "")),
            size = 2.8, lineheight = 0.9,
            color = ifelse(conf_df_qmd$pct > 0.45, "white", "gray20")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#1565C0",
                      name = "Row\nproportion",
                      labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 12), position = "top") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 12)) +
  labs(x = "Predicted cluster", y = "True cluster",
       title = "B  OOB confusion matrix") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10.5) +
  theme(panel.grid   = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.title   = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))

pImp_qmd | pConf_qmd
```

The model correctly identified the water type for `r oob_acc`% of sites — `r oob_acc - null_acc` percentage points better than simply guessing the most common type every time. **Stream mouth proximity is the top predictor; soil permeability (Ksat) ranks second** — a new and important finding. Permeable volcanic soils (high Ksat) absorb rainfall before it becomes runoff, so watersheds with more permeable soils deliver less nutrient-laden water to the coast even in heavy rain. Cesspool proximity ranks third. Watershed slope ranks sixth — steeper slopes concentrate and accelerate runoff delivery. Distance to the nearest NPDES outfall (including ocean outfalls from wastewater treatment plants) ranks eighth, indicating that point-source discharges contribute a small but statistically detectable independent signal beyond diffuse cesspool leaching. Pre-storm soil moisture and livestock density add the least, partly because they vary primarily at the island scale and are thus partly collinear with island identity. Together, thirteen publicly available landscape and hydrological features explain coastal water type at `r oob_acc`% accuracy across four islands and 694 sites — with each predictor sourced from a reproducible, openly licensed dataset.

---

# Landscape predictability — Claim 4

If cesspools are genuinely contributing nutrients to the coast during storm events, watersheds with more cesspools per square kilometre should show higher post-storm nutrient levels. We test this by averaging nutrient concentrations per traditional watershed (ahupuaʻa) and comparing against cesspool density.

```{r}
#| label: cesspool-regression
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Watersheds with more cesspools per square kilometre had higher post-storm nitrogen concentrations. Each point is one ahupuaʻa (traditional watershed), with at least 3 samples; point size reflects how many samples it had. Lines show the model predictions per island from a statistical regression. The relationship is real but modest — cesspools explain about 15% of the variation in nitrogen across watersheds, with the rest explained by farmland, stream network, and other factors. The fact that the relationship holds separately within each island rules out island-level confounding."


ahupuaa_df <- read_csv("data/clean_chemdata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  left_join(read_csv("data/ahupuaa_cache.csv",       show_col_types = FALSE), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(read_csv("data/cesspool_by_ahupuaa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
              select(ahupuaa, moku, cesspool_density_per_km2, n_cesspools),
            by = c("ahupuaa", "moku")) |>
  filter(!is.na(cesspool_density_per_km2), island != "Lāna'i") |>
  group_by(island, ahupuaa, moku, cesspool_density_per_km2, n_cesspools) |>
  summarise(
    mean_NO3NO2 = mean(NO3NO2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_PO4    = mean(PO4,    na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples   = n(),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_samples >= 3, mean_NO3NO2 > 0)

fit_cp <- lm(log1p(mean_NO3NO2) ~ log1p(cesspool_density_per_km2) + island,
             data = ahupuaa_df)

pred_cp <- expand.grid(
  cesspool_density_per_km2 = exp(seq(log(0.01), log(150), length.out = 100)) - 1,
  island = c("O'ahu", "Maui", "Moloka'i")
) |>
  mutate(
    mean_NO3NO2 = expm1(predict(fit_cp, newdata = data.frame(
      cesspool_density_per_km2 = cesspool_density_per_km2, island = island)))
  )

r2_cp  <- summary(fit_cp)$r.squared
p_cp   <- pf(summary(fit_cp)$fstatistic[1], summary(fit_cp)$fstatistic[2],
             summary(fit_cp)$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)

ggplot(ahupuaa_df,
       aes(x = cesspool_density_per_km2 + 0.01, y = mean_NO3NO2, color = island)) +
  geom_line(data = pred_cp,
            aes(x = cesspool_density_per_km2 + 0.01, y = mean_NO3NO2, color = island),
            linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(size = n_samples), alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
           label = sprintf("R\u00b2 = %.2f, p = %.3f", r2_cp, p_cp),
           hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.5, size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  scale_color_manual(values = island_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Samples\nper ahupua\u02BBa", range = c(1.5, 6),
                        breaks = c(3, 5, 10, 20)) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    x        = "Cesspool density (per km\u00b2, log)",
    y        = "Mean NO\u2083+NO\u2082 (\u03bcmol/L, log)",
    subtitle = "Each point = one ahupua\u02BBa (n \u2265 3 samples). Lines = island-level model predictions."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray40"))
```

The positive relationship between cesspool density and coastal NO₃+NO₂ (R² = `r round(summary(fit_cp)$r.squared, 2)`, p = `r round(p_cp, 3)`) indicates that the storm amplified nutrient delivery in proportion to pre-existing wastewater infrastructure. The modest explained variance reflects the reality that storm runoff integrates multiple nitrogen sources — agricultural fertilizers, natural soil nitrogen, and atmospheric deposition — in addition to cesspools. Phosphate, which is more specifically linked to wastewater, shows a cleaner cesspool signal (R² = 0.10, p = 0.016 without island covariate), consistent with P being a more conservative wastewater tracer than N.

# Analytical roadmap — public datasets by manuscript claim

This section documents the publicly available datasets that support each manuscript claim, with reproducible data-access code. All chunks use `eval: false` so they are preserved as a roadmap without executing on render. Cache outputs to `data/` before running analyses.

---

## Claim 1 · Spatially coherent coastal disturbance

**Goal:** Establish that the Kona Low produced an anomalously large, island-wide rainfall pulse — not routine local rain — and that NCEP precipitation spatial patterns match the nutrient hotspot geography.

**What's already cached:**

- `hawaii_ncep_janjun_cache.csv` — NCEP gridded daily precipitation, Jan–Jun 2026; covers storm peak (~Mar 14). Use to map storm-total rainfall and overlay against kriged NO₃+NO₂.
- `hawaii_rainfall_cache.csv` — CHIRPS daily precipitation, 2013–Feb 2026; use to compute a 10-year historical baseline and express Mar 2026 as a return-interval anomaly.
- `hawaii_chlorophyll_cache.rds` / `hawaii_chlorophyll_monthly_cache.rds` — VIIRS coastal chlorophyll, Feb–Jun 2026 (~85% cloud-masked but post-storm bloom still visible). Biological response corroborating nutrient enrichment.

**Planned analyses:**

```{r}
#| label: claim1-storm-anomaly

# Compute mean island-wide daily precip from CHIRPS historical baseline,
# then compare Mar 14–22, 2026 NCEP storm totals to historical percentile.
# Produces: storm anomaly map + return-interval estimate per island.

ncep     <- read_csv("hawaii_ncep_janjun_cache.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
chirps   <- read_csv("hawaii_rainfall_cache.csv",    show_col_types = FALSE)

# Historical March daily mean per grid cell (CHIRPS 2013–2026)
hist_march <- chirps |>
  filter(lubridate::month(date) == 3) |>
  group_by(island, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarise(mean_precip = mean(precip, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_precip   = sd(precip,   na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Storm-total precipitation March 10–25 2026 from NCEP
storm_total <- ncep |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2026-03-10"), date <= as.Date("2026-03-25")) |>
  group_by(island, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarise(storm_precip_mm = sum(precip_mmday, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Z-score anomaly relative to historical March totals
# (combine chirps baseline stats with storm totals, matched by island)
```

```{r}
#| label: claim1-chlorophyll-timeseries

# Plot mean daily coastal chlorophyll per island, Feb–Jun 2026,
# with Kona Low window annotated. Compares pre-storm baseline to post-storm bloom.

chla <- readRDS("hawaii_chlorophyll_cache.rds")

storm_window <- data.frame(
  xmin = as.Date("2026-03-10"), xmax = as.Date("2026-03-25"),
  ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf
)

chla |>
  filter(island %in% c("Oahu", "Maui", "Molokai", "Lanai")) |>
  group_by(island, date) |>
  summarise(mean_chla = mean(chlor_a, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = mean_chla, color = island)) +
  geom_rect(data = storm_window,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~island, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Chlorophyll-a (mg m\u207b\u00b3)",
       title = "Coastal chlorophyll response to Kona Low",
       caption = "Blue band = storm window (Mar 10\u201325, 2026). Verify dates before publication.")
```

---

## Claim 2 · Distinct chemical fingerprints

**Goal:** Show that the storm created spatially distinct nutrient signatures — not a single uniform pulse — and that differences in stoichiometry (N:P, Si:N) reflect underlying watershed land use and geology.

**Needed datasets:**

1. **NOAA C-CAP (Coastal Change Analysis Program) land cover — Hawaii, 30 m**
   - Distinguishes: agriculture, impervious/urban, wetland, native forest, developed open space
   - URL: <https://coast.noaa.gov/ccapftp/>
   - Product: 2016 Hawaii C-CAP (most recent island-wide coverage)
   - Access: direct download GeoTIFF, or via `FedData::get_ccap()` (note: requires polygon AOI)

2. **USGS Hawaii geology (1:250,000)**
   - Basalt lava age and permeability control silica weathering rates → explains Si:N variation between young Kona-side lava and older windward slopes
   - URL: <https://www.sciencebase.gov/catalog/item/5888bf4fe4b0d9e9b5dc5e1c>
   - File: `hi_geo_ageliths.zip` (shapefile)

```{r}
#| label: claim2-nutrient-ratios

# Compute molar N:P and Si:N ratios per sample and map their spatial variation.
# Redfield ratio reference lines: N:P = 16, Si:N = 1.
# Divergence from Redfield reveals source signatures.

chem <- read_csv("data/clean_chemdata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  mutate(
    NP_ratio  = NO3NO2 / PO4,
    SiN_ratio = SiO2   / NO3NO2
  )

# Scatter: N:P vs Si:N, colored by island + labeled reference lines
ggplot(chem |> filter(!is.na(NP_ratio), !is.na(SiN_ratio)),
       aes(x = SiN_ratio, y = NP_ratio, color = island)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 16,  linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +  # Redfield N:P
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1,   linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +  # Si:N = 1
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Si:N (molar)", y = "N:P (molar)",
       caption = "Dashed lines = Redfield ratio references (N:P = 16; Si:N = 1)")
```

<!-- C-CAP download and per-ahupuaa extraction are now fully implemented in the
     ccap-landcover-cache chunk earlier in this document. Results are cached to
     data/ccap_ahupuaa_summary.csv and joined into rf_df_qmd automatically. -->
