## Claim 3 · Increased watershed–coast connectivity

**Goal:** Directly measure storm runoff by pulling USGS stream gauge discharge records for Oʻahu and Maui. Peak discharge on March 14–15 corroborates the nutrient–salinity dilution signal and closes the mechanistic chain: rainfall → discharge → coastal salinity drop → nutrient enrichment.

**Needed dataset: USGS NWIS stream discharge**

- Package: `dataRetrieval` (CRAN)
- Parameter code: `00060` (discharge, ft³/s)
- Daily values (`readNWISdv`) or instantaneous (`readNWISuv` for 15-min data during storm)

```{r}
#| label: claim3-gauge-discovery
#| eval: false
# Find all active Hawaii stream gauges with discharge data
hi_gauges <- whatNWISsites(
  stateCd       = "HI",
  parameterCd   = "00060",
  hasDataTypeCd = "dv"
)

# Focus: Oahu and Maui gauges
hi_gauges |>
  filter(stringr::str_detect(station_nm, regex("oahu|maui|wailuku|manoa|nuuanu|waimea|iao",
                                               ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  select(site_no, station_nm, dec_lat_va, dec_long_va, drain_area_va)
```

```{r}
#| label: claim3-discharge-pull
#| eval: false
# Pull daily discharge for key gauges, Jan–Apr 2026.
# Known active Oahu gauges (verify currency with whatNWISsites above):
#   16211600 — Manoa Stream at Manoa   (urban/residential watershed)
#   16240500 — Nuuanu Reservoir (urban)
#   16330000 — Waimea River (rural/agricultural)
# Known Maui gauges:
#   16400000 — Wailuku River at Kahului
#   16508000 — Waihee River

gauge_ids <- c("16211600", "16240500", "16330000",  # Oahu
               "16400000", "16508000")               # Maui

discharge_raw <- readNWISdv(
  siteNumbers  = gauge_ids,
  parameterCd  = "00060",
  startDate    = "2026-01-01",
  endDate      = "2026-04-15"
) |>
  renameNWISColumns()

# Save immediately
saveRDS(discharge_raw, "data/usgs_discharge_cache.rds")

# Quick plot — discharge over time with storm window
storm_window <- data.frame(xmin = as.Date("2026-03-10"), xmax = as.Date("2026-03-25"))
discharge_raw |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Date, y = Flow, color = site_no)) +
  geom_rect(data = storm_window,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~site_no, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Discharge (ft\u00b3/s)")
```

```{r}
#| label: claim3-nwis-wq-note
#| eval: false
# NOTE (July 2026): The USGS NWIS discrete water-quality service ("qw") has been
# retired. readNWISqw() and readNWISdata(service="qw") no longer work.
# Use the Water Quality Portal instead — query USGS sites by site number via WQP:
#
#   readWQPdata(siteid = paste0("USGS-", c("16211600","16400000","16508000")),
#               characteristicName = c("Nitrate + Nitrite","Phosphate","Silica"),
#               startDateLo = "2010-01-01", startDateHi = "2026-04-30")
#
# This returns discrete grab samples collected at the gauges during both
# baseflow and storm conditions, allowing direct storm amplification estimates.
```

```{r}
#| label: claim3-discharge-vs-nutrients
#| eval: false
# After pulling discharge: compare peak storm discharge per watershed
# to mean nutrient concentration at sampling sites within that watershed.
# Requires joining gauge sites to ahupuaʻa assignments (by spatial proximity).
# Expects: discharge_raw saved above, chem with ahupuaa column

discharge <- readRDS("data/usgs_discharge_cache.rds") |>
  renameNWISColumns()

# Peak discharge in storm window per gauge
peak_q <- discharge |>
  filter(Date >= as.Date("2026-03-10"), Date <= as.Date("2026-03-25")) |>
  group_by(site_no) |>
  summarise(peak_discharge_cfs = max(Flow, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# TODO: spatial join gauge locations to ahupuaʻa, then join to mean nutrient
# loading per ahupuaʻa from chem data
```

---

## Claim 4 · Predictability from landscape structure

**Goal:** Show that spatial variation in nutrient concentrations is predictable from pre-existing landscape features (cesspool density, impervious cover, watershed area, stream density). A simple regression or random forest of nutrient loading ~ landscape predictors would make this quantitative.

**What's already available:**

- `data/cesspool_by_ahupuaa.csv` — cesspool count and density per ahupuaʻa (already in use)
- `data/sample_cesspool_distances.csv` — distance from each sample to nearest cesspool

**Needed: NOAA C-CAP (see Claim 2 above) + USGS NHDPlus stream network**

```{r}
#| label: claim4-nhd-download
#| eval: false
# Download NHDPlus (National Hydrography Dataset) for Hawaii.
# Use to compute: stream density (km/km²) per ahupuaʻa watershed.
# Dense stream networks = more efficient nutrient routing to coast.
# Package: nhdplusTools

# Hawaii is in USGS Region 20 (Pacific Islands)
# Download NHDPlus HR for Hawaii
hi_nhd_url <- "https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Hydrography/NHDPlusHR/Beta/GDB/NHDPLUS_H_2001_HU4_GDB.zip"
# Alternative: use nhdplusTools::get_nhdplus() with AOI polygon

ahupuaa_sf <- sf::st_read("data/ahupuaa_boundaries.geojson", quiet = TRUE)

# Get flowlines within Oahu bounding box as a test
oahu_bbox <- ahupuaa_sf |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(mokupuni, regex("oahu", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  sf::st_bbox() |>
  sf::st_as_sfc() |>
  sf::st_as_sf()

flowlines <- nhdplusTools::get_nhdplus(AOI = oahu_bbox, realization = "flowline")
saveRDS(flowlines, "data/nhd_oahu_flowlines.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: claim4-landscape-regression
#| eval: false
# Regression: mean NO3+NO2 per ahupuaʻa ~ cesspool_density + pct_impervious
# + stream_density + watershed_area
# Requires: ccap_by_ahupuaa.csv (from Claim 2) and nhd stream density (above)

chem_aug <- read_csv("data/clean_chemdata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(island)) |>
  left_join(read_csv("data/ahupuaa_cache.csv",      show_col_types = FALSE), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(read_csv("data/cesspool_by_ahupuaa.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
              select(ahupuaa, moku, cesspool_density_per_km2),
            by = c("ahupuaa", "moku"))

# Mean nutrient loading per ahupuaʻa
ahupuaa_nutrients <- chem_aug |>
  group_by(island, ahupuaa, moku, cesspool_density_per_km2) |>
  summarise(
    mean_NO3NO2  = mean(NO3NO2,  na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_PO4     = mean(PO4,     na.rm = TRUE),
    n_samples    = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(n_samples >= 3)  # only ahupuaʻa with enough samples

# Simple log-log regression (add ccap and nhd predictors when available)
lm(log1p(mean_NO3NO2) ~ log1p(cesspool_density_per_km2), data = ahupuaa_nutrients) |>
  summary()
```

---

## Claim 5 · community science enabled detection

**Goal:** Quantify the monitoring gap — show that conventional water quality monitoring in Hawaiʻi would not have captured this event at the spatial or temporal resolution needed. Two lines of evidence: (1) spatial coverage comparison, (2) sampling timing relative to storm.

**Needed dataset: EPA Water Quality Portal (WQP)**

- Package: `dataRetrieval` (same package as USGS NWIS)
- Function: `readWQPdata()` — returns all water quality records for a state/date range
- Coverage: includes Hawaii DOH, NOAA, EPA BEACH Act, university monitoring programs

```{r}
#| label: claim5-wqp-query
#| eval: false
# Query all Hawaii coastal nutrient samples from WQP in the 60 days
# surrounding the storm. Compare: how many samples? At how many unique sites?
# How close to shore? How soon after the storm?

wqp_hi <- readWQPdata(
  statecode      = "US:15",          # Hawaii FIPS
  characteristicName = c("Nitrate", "Nitrate + Nitrite", "Phosphate",
                         "Silica", "Specific conductance"),
  startDateLo    = "2026-02-01",
  startDateHi    = "2026-05-01"
)

# Cache immediately — API calls can be slow
saveRDS(wqp_hi, "data/wqp_hawaii_cache.rds")

# Summary: how many unique sites, samples, and dates near storm window?
wqp_hi |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(ActivityStartDate)) |>
  summarise(
    n_samples      = n(),
    n_sites        = n_distinct(MonitoringLocationIdentifier),
    n_storm_window = sum(between(date, as.Date("2026-03-10"), as.Date("2026-04-15")),
                         na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: claim5-coverage-map
#| eval: false
# Map conventional monitoring sites (WQP) vs community science sites (chem)
# to visualize the spatial coverage gap.
# Expects: wqp_hi cached above

wqp_hi   <- readRDS("data/wqp_hawaii_cache.rds")
chem     <- read_csv("data/clean_chemdata.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ahupuaa  <- sf::st_read("data/ahupuaa_boundaries.geojson", quiet = TRUE)

# WQP sites as sf
wqp_sf <- wqp_hi |>
  distinct(MonitoringLocationIdentifier, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(LongitudeMeasure), !is.na(LatitudeMeasure)) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("LongitudeMeasure", "LatitudeMeasure"), crs = 4326) |>
  mutate(source = "Conventional monitoring")

# community science sites as sf
cs_sf <- chem |>
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326) |>
  mutate(source = "community science (this study)")


# Hawaii land for background
hi_land <- ahupuaa |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(mokupuni,
    regex("oahu|maui|molokai|lanai", ignore_case = TRUE))) |>
  sf::st_union() |> sf::st_as_sf()

# Combined map
bind_rows(
  wqp_sf |> select(source, geometry),
  cs_sf  |> select(source, geometry)
) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = hi_land, fill = "gray80", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(aes(color = source, size = source), alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Conventional monitoring"   = "firebrick",
                                "community science (this study)" = "#1565C0")) +
  scale_size_manual(values  = c("Conventional monitoring"   = 2.5,
                                "community science (this study)" = 1.0)) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Spatial monitoring coverage: conventional vs. community science")
```
